TypeSafe's **Jev**, the first public **System One model**, answers typed questions about state your
application supplies. State is the text, images, and application data your code sends with a
request. Jev can answer a Choice among options, a Noul (the probability that a statement is true), a
Score on levels you describe, or a Box that locates something in an image. Each answer comes back as
typed data with calibrated probabilities, for your code to use.

The rest of this skill is guidance: patterns that tend to produce reliable integrations. None of it
is absolute. Models change, applications differ, and edge cases exist. When a situation calls for
something else, test the alternative and use your judgment.

## Judgments from Jev, decisions in code

Integrations tend to work best when Jev makes the judgments and code decides what to do with
them. Think of each decision as a **truth table**. Jev supplies the inputs, such as "Does the
customer sound frustrated?" or "Which product is the message about?". Code holds the logic that
maps those inputs to an action.

A question that asks Jev to make the decision, such as "Should this ticket be escalated?" or "What
should the agent do next?", usually means the question is at the wrong layer. Instead, break the
decision into the judgments it depends on, and write the decision itself in code, where it's
visible and testable. Writing out the table often shows gaps in the business logic too. A
combination of judgments with no defined outcome is a design question about the system, and it is
best settled in code.

## Live docs

The live docs are the source of truth for request syntax, SDKs, question types, limits, and current
model behavior. Read the relevant pages as part of the task.

- Start at the [documentation index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt). Append `.md` to a page
  path to get the page as Markdown, and resolve relative links against `https://docs.typesafe.ai`.
- Exact request and response schemas: the [OpenAPI spec](https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json) and
  the [HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/api.md) page. For an SDK, see the
  [Python](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/python-sdk.md) or
  [JavaScript](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/js-sdk.md) page and the types in the installed package.
- Question types: [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/primitives.md) and each type's own page,
  [structured instructions and criteria](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/advanced.md), and
  [images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/images.md).
- Models, context limits, and rate limits: [models](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/models.md). Known
  model weak spots and their workarounds are on the
  [jaggedness page](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/jaggedness.md).
- Architecture: [how to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/how-to-build.md),
  [patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/patterns.md), and
  [cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/cookbooks.md). The cookbook closest to your use case is a
  good starting point for a new workflow.

If you can't reach the live docs, use the installed SDK's types or local docs, and tell the user
you did. Leave out details that depend on the version rather than guessing them.

## Workflow

1. **Start from the decision logic.** Begin with what the application will show, select, change,
   or hand off. Sketch the truth table or rules that decide it, and list the inputs they need.
   Inputs that need an understanding of language or images make good questions. Arithmetic, dates,
   exact lookups, and policy usually belong in code. Aim for every question to feed the table, and
   give every combination of answers an outcome, including the case where a Noul lands between your
   thresholds. If code alone can already make the decision reliably, tell the user.
2. **Keep all question wording in one place.** Questions, options, criteria, and thresholds are the
   parts of an integration people audit and edit most. Keeping them together in one module makes
   that easier. [Design the state](#design-the-state) and
   [Write the questions](#write-the-questions) describe what tends to work.
3. **Probe the live API**: send test requests as described in
   [Test with the live API](#test-with-the-live-api). Use representative cases, hard cases, and
   negative cases. Keep going until the application behaves as intended.
4. **Integrate.** A few habits help here. Expose or log the exact request payload. When a call to
   the API fails, surface it as an error, not as an answer; for example, don't treat a failed call
   as a "no". Keep API keys on the server.

If the user's request is open-ended, offer the few directions from [Cookbooks](#cookbooks) that
best serve their goal, and recommend one. If the request is concrete, build it.

## Design the state

A useful check for any question is the **human test**: could a smart person, shown only this state
and this question, answer quickly by intuition? When a question fails the test, the fix is usually
in the state, not in the wording.

- **Give what a person would look at.** That means who sent each message, the full thread rather
  than a truncated last line, names rather than raw IDs or @-mention markup, and the item the
  question is about rather than the whole catalogue. State facts your code already knows, such as
  "all messages in `replies` were sent after the refund was issued", rather than leaving the model
  to work them out again.
- **Supply facts the model may lack**, such as what an internal product name or codename refers
  to.
- **Ensure every field in the state is relevant.** Irrelevant detail clutters the context and
  reduces accuracy. A field added for one question can sway the answer to another, and the model
  can read an empty list as a signal.
- **Be mindful when truncating.** Truncate long strings only when you need to, and check that the
  cut doesn't remove context the questions need.
- **Structure with named fields.** JSON objects with descriptive keys work better than a string of
  serialized JSON. They also let a question refer to each part by its path. Stable names such as
  `candidates.refund_policy` are easier to refer to than array positions.
- **Consider leaving out what no person could judge**, such as an unreadable crop or a distinction
  experts dispute. The model's answer there tends to be noise, and code will treat that noise as
  signal.

## Write the questions

Break complex judgments or decisions into their parts, and combine the answers in code with
weighted sums, boolean logic, thresholds, or other heuristics to reach the final decision. For
example, rather than asking "Is this fraud?" or "Is this spam?", ask the set of atomic questions
about what might make something fraud or spam. Each question tends to work best when it asks for
**one judgment** that a person could make at a glance.

- **Ask the concrete, observable thing.** Aim for something a person could point to: "Is a SQL
  query built by string concatenation here?" rather than "Are there SQL injection risks?".
- **One judgment per question; beware the "or".** Two conditions joined by "or" or "and" usually
  work better as two questions. Likewise, a list of rules usually works better as one question per
  rule.
- **Anchor intent to the goal.** When the judgment is about what someone wants, it helps to name
  their goal: "Which of these files does the user want copied?" rather than "Which of these names
  the main input?".
- **Name the subject directly.** "Where is the coffee mug in `photo`?" reads better than "Where is
  `target` in `photo`?" with the target defined somewhere else. Context that only one question
  needs, including an image, usually fits best in that question's instructions (the question text)
  or its criteria (the descriptions of its options, its levels, or what yes and no mean). Context
  that many questions share can go in the state once, and each question can refer to it by its
  exact path in backticks. When you ask the same question about many items, it usually works better
  to put each item into its own question than to give an ID the model has to look up in a shared
  list.
- **Each question is answered on its own.** Questions in a request can't see each other or each
  other's answers. Any context a question relies on belongs in the state or in that question.
- **Write plainly.** A question isn't an LLM prompt. Preambles, "consider X, Y, and Z" lists, and
  output-format instructions add noise. Descriptions of the options belong in the criteria, not in
  the question. Phrase the question so that a true answer means yes. Watch for double negatives,
  and for presuppositions such as "the next step".
- **Name the case that causes confusion.** If answers keep mixing up two outcomes, say in the
  criteria what separates them, using the specific case. For example, for "Is this a refund
  request?", note that a question about the refund policy is not a request. A vague exclusion such
  as "not other kinds of message" helps less, and can draw attention to the wrong answer.

### Criteria

- **Ask about the null case separately.** A Box always returns a location and a Choice always picks
  an option, even when nothing fits. Pair either one with a Noul in the same request that asks
  whether anything fits ("Is there a coffee mug in `photo`?", "Does `message` name any of our
  products?"), so code can tell when nothing does. As of Jev 1.14, this companion Noul usually works
  better than a "none of the above" option.
- **Option names are sent to the model; question IDs are not.** Names that describe the content
  (`refund_request`, `shipping_delay`) help the model. Positional names (`A`, `left`, `option_1`)
  give it nothing meaningful to go on and can bias the answer.
- **Keep options distinct and concrete.** Wording that options share with each other, or with the
  input, can pull probability toward those options. An option that covers several meanings is
  often worth splitting, because its probability can't tell code which meaning applied. Direction
  and magnitude usually work better as separate questions, so that the answer to one doesn't get
  mixed into the other.
- **Describe each Score level as a situation.** Each level should make sense when read on its own:
  "The customer mentions a minor inconvenience" rather than "More upset than the previous level".
- **Describe a Noul's `false` criterion as a concrete situation**, such as "the package arrived on
  time", rather than as "not late".
- **Use a Noul per statement when more than one can be true.** A Choice picks one option, so a
  message that is both a refund request and a complaint forces it to split probability between the
  two. Separate Nouls let each one be true on its own.

## Compose requests

**Bundle questions that share state.** A handy heuristic: if two calls would send the same state
with different questions, they can likely be one call. Questions are cheap and run in parallel, and
the state is read and paid for once. See
[parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md).

**Ask speculatively**, meaning ask a question before you know whether you'll need its answer. A
question that only matters in some cases can go in the same request as the question that
identifies the case. Ask "Is `order` a return request?" and "Which item in `order.items` is being
returned?" together, and have code read the second answer only when the first is yes. The second
question doesn't need an "if" clause, because code handles the condition. See
[speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md).

A second request is usually worth it when:

- code needs an answer to build the next state, fetch evidence, or choose the next options;
- a state field needed for one question measurably misleads another;
- different sets of questions need to be cached or versioned separately.

## Read the answers

### Confidence is rarely the gate

Naive implementations often use an answer's `confidence` as the check that decides whether code
acts. Confidence measures how concentrated an answer's probability distribution is, which is not
the same as how likely the answer is to be correct. Think about what the probabilities should look
like in your use case; another calculation over them may suit it better.

### Probabilities and thresholds

- **A probability is the likelihood that an answer is correct.** Jev isn't a calculator for
  probability problems. Ask it for judgments, and do any math on odds or probabilities in code. A
  Noul near 0.5 usually means the state doesn't settle the question.
- **The top answer is a good default**: the Choice's top option, or the Score's position.
- **0.7 and 0.3 make good starting thresholds for a Noul**: above 0.7 reads as yes, below 0.3 as no,
  and the band between means the question isn't settled, which can get its own row in the truth
  table. Adjust them when the application calls for it, and be wary of over-fitting them to a
  handful of test cases.
- **Look at Score distributions.** The Score's position can get pulled toward the middle and hide
  two-peaked answers, so look at the level probabilities before deciding which value your code
  reads.

## Test with the live API

Sending test requests to the live API is a great way to test questions against your data. Ask the
user for permission first. Get a budget for experimentation (TypeSafe is very inexpensive, so a
little can go a very long way), disclose what data will be sent (point out any personal or private
data), and say that their `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` will be used.

- Start with a few representative cases, plus hard ones and some whose answer is "no" or "nothing
  fits".
- Compare wordings by sending each variant as a separate question in one request, over the same
  state.
- Read individual answers, not only aggregates.
- Keep the exact request payload for each case so any result can be rerun.
- Check each change against cases you didn't use while tuning.

Make sure any agent that sends test requests has network access to the API endpoint.

### When an answer looks wrong

Check these, in this order:

1. the payload as actually sent;
2. the state, against the human test;
3. the options and candidates: is the right answer among them?
4. the scope of the questions: can each one be broken down into smaller judgments?
5. the wording.

If a clear question with complete state still gets an answer you're confident is wrong, check the
jaggedness page for the model you're using. It lists known weak spots and how to work around them.
If the behavior isn't listed, the TypeSafe team welcomes examples through the channel linked on
that page. In the meantime, work out an alternative approach with the user that avoids the weak
spot.

### Yellow flags

Typically, a good change is one that makes the definition clearer or improves the state. Check each
change on cases you didn't tune on. Wording written to produce a particular value is **prompt
gymnastics**, and it tends to break on new inputs and on the next model version. Some yellow flags:

- criteria that name specific test items, or that gain a clause for each failing case;
- caveats that explain away a model quirk;
- thresholds fitted to particular cases;
- tests that assert an exact probability;
- code that quietly overrides answers.

The structural fix is usually better state, a separate question, or code.

## Cookbooks

Each of these starting points combines questions to serve one goal. Ideas outside this list are
welcome.

- **Route and fill arguments.** One request identifies what the user is asking for and which
  values go in each argument. Code then calls the handler. See
  [function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md) and
  [intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md).
- **Select instead of generate.** Code finds candidate values or spans of text, the model picks
  the intended one, and code copies or normalizes it. See
  [value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md),
  [date extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/date_extraction_cookbook.md), and
  [structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md).
- **Find and judge evidence.** Retrieve candidates and ask how relevant each one is. See
  [line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md),
  [re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md), and
  [classifying RAG passages](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classifying_rag_passages.md).
- **Turn answers into data.** Score each dimension once, then let code or users change the weights
  and views. If you have labeled outcomes, the answers can become features for a model. See
  [composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and
  [feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md).
- **Verify and escalate.** Check claims or fields against their evidence, and send the cases that
  fail to a person or a reasoning model. See
  [citation checks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) and
  [extraction cascades](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md).

The TypeSafe team is constantly adding cookbooks of well-tested patterns to the live documentation.
It's a good idea to check the [cookbooks index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/go/cookbooks.md) for one
that fits the problem you're solving.

> How to use TypeSafe's System One API

- [Introduction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction.md): Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model. Send state and typed questions; get structured answers your code can use directly.
- [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md): Get up and running with Jev in 5 minutes.
- [Jev with coding agents](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/coding-agents.md): What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.
- [Example use cases](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/use-case-map.md): Explore TypeSafe use cases by industry and turn promising ideas into software workflows.
- [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md): System One models make fast, structured decisions for software. Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first System One model.
- [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md): What state is, how to structure it, and how to give a System One model the context it needs.
- [Primitives (Questions)](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives.md): The TypeSafe question types, the typed answers they return, how to choose between them, and how to ask several at once.
- [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md): A Choice is a System One question type for selecting one option from a defined set. The answer includes the selected option, a probability for each option, and confidence.
- [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md): A Score is a System One question type for rating content against ordered, descriptive levels. The answer includes a score, a probability for each level, and confidence.
- [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md): A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.
- [Box](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/box.md): A Box is a System One question type for finding where something is in an image. The answer is the four edges of a box around it, as fractions of the image's width and height.
- [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md): Instructions, Choice options, Score levels, and Noul criteria all accept JSON structure.
- [Images](https://docs.typesafe.ai/images.md): Send images in a System One request: in the state, inside a question's instructions, and as the criteria a question is judged against.
- [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md): How TypeSafe reports certainty, how it differs from probability, and how to use it to control system behavior.
- [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md): Design AI-powered software by keeping code in control and giving System One narrow, structured decisions.
- [AI primer](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md): Why TypeSafe trains decision models with calibrated probabilities instead of optimizing for generated text.
- [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md): Architectural patterns for building systems with TypeSafe.
- [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md): Send many questions in a single request, including speculative ones, and let your code decide what's relevant.
- [Confidence-gated routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/confidence-routing.md): Use confidence as a second axis. The answer tells you what; confidence tells you whether to act.
- [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md): Break a complex judgment into atomic scores, combine with weights you control in code.
- [Intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md): Classify incoming requests and route each to the optimal handler: deterministic logic, a specialist LLM, or a human.
- [Cookbooks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks.md): End-to-end recipes that show TypeSafe in real problems, from a few questions to full pipelines.
- [Function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md): Turns natural-language trading requests into calls to ordinary typed functions by mapping function names and closed-set arguments to confidence-aware TypeSafe questions.
- [Skill suggestion](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion.md): Picks at most one skill for an agent turn out of the 182 in Nous Research's Hermes catalog, using two TypeSafe requests to rank and re-check the top candidates.
- [Guardrails for LLMs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/llm_guardrails.md): Screen every message going into and out of an LLM app with one TypeSafe request, thresholding hazard probabilities and severity to pass, review, block, or route.
- [Double-checking citations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md): Catch wrong or hallucinated citations by checking against the source document. One Choice question decides whether the quote's context supports the claim.

- [Simple memory system](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/basic_memory.md): Let Jev decide which requests and answers are worth remembering, then wrap the Jev call in a small function that adds memories to later calls.
- [Hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md): Classifies documents through deep patent, retail product, biomedical, and source-code hierarchies using parallel beam search over TypeSafe Choice probabilities.
- [Classification using confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/classification_using_confidence.md): Classify SEC annual reports into 75 industry groups with one Choice each, then read the answer's own confidence to decide whether to report that group or the broader division above it.
- [Twitch chat filter](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/twitch_chat_filter.md): Hides insults, spam, and unasked-for gameplay tips in Twitch chat, blurs spoilers, and highlights questions. Each message gets one TypeSafe request with three questions, requests run concurrently, and plain rules in code turn the answers into what the viewer sees.
- [SDE cascade](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md): Uses a 2-stage structured-data-extraction cascade (mini → verify → reasoning) to get most of the quality of a big reasoning model at a fraction of the cost.

- [Reading a scanned vaccination record](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/reading_scanned_documents.md): Find each vaccine on a scanned travel record with a Noul and a Box, read the year of each dose with a Choice that can answer unreadable, and check each dose still covers the trip in a text-only request.
- [OCR confidence and bounding boxes](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/ocr_confidence_bounding_boxes.md): Check the values an OCR extractor read from invoice photos: Jev boxes each value, scores it against the page and against a crop of its box, and flags low scores for review.
- [Feeder-cam visit log](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/feeder_watch.md): Send frames from bird feeder camera footage to Jev with five questions, one of them a Box that finds the bird, then use plain code to turn the answers into a visit log per species.

- [Intelliprompter](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/intelliprompter.md): Tick off a presenter's notes as they speak: TypeSafe scores the live transcript against each note not yet covered, and a note stays ticked once its score passes the threshold.

- [Self-consistency: nouls](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md): Route uncertain probabilities to human review while keeping the underlying noul values visible.

"""Jev strategy review: Jev judges atomic questions; this file decides.

All state, question wording, criteria and thresholds live here, so the review
can be audited and rerun. Usage: python3 review/jev_strategy.py [--send]
Without --send it only writes the payload. Needs TYPESAFE_API_KEY.
"""
import json, os, sys, urllib.request, pathlib

10→OUT = pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name("out")
YES, NO = 0.7, 0.3  # skill starting thresholds; the band between is "unsettled"

STATE = {
    "event": "Meta Model API hackathon, Indie Dev Track, 10 days, solo founder using an AI coding agent. "
             "Projects are expected to build with Meta's models (Muse Spark). A Y Combinator application is due 2026-11-02.",
    "thesis": "A self-contained identity that acts and can prove what it did: it builds infrastructure for a business, "
              "every action is authorised against its capabilities, leaves a tamper-evident receipt, and is anchored "
              "on a blockchain so anyone can verify who did what under what authority.",
    "pitch_concepts": ["self-contained identity container", "first-person embodiment with a talking avatar",
20→                       "kernel-peer admission over a Unix socket", "typed operation filesystem (3tchedFS)",
                       "OSCAL catalog, profiles and tag routing", "boundary rules compiled into capability grants and OpenFlow policy",
                       "compliant-by-construction CMS with PII redaction", "Web3 index with Merkle root anchored on-chain",
                       "root identity without execution rights", "two human approvals for root actions",
                       "delegation to agents by attenuation", "subsidiaries as Linux users bounded by home directories",
                       "Florida LLC declaration schema"],
    "golden_path": ["avatar speaks a fixed introduction script",
                    "user asks it to create a CMS for one business from one declaration and one OSCAL profile",
                    "the identity provisions one or two real things through its own filesystem operations, with a visible trace",
                    "each action returns a receipt with operation id and chain event hash",
30→                    "one receipt is anchored on-chain",
                    "a judge verifies the anchored receipt themselves"],
    "proven": ["identity container runs with its own filesystem mount; a read operation through it returned the identity with an operation id and chain events",
               "the bridge identifies the calling container from the kernel and checks an exact capability per operation",
               "infrastructure operations (create container, create network bridge) are exposed to the identity but have not been run in the demo",
               "the identity has internet-only networking and no network path to the backend",
               "chat goes through the router to a hosted model (currently a Qwen model, not Meta)",
               "the avatar speaks the fixed intro and takes spoken questions"],
    "planned": ["Meta model wired into the router", "OSCAL catalog and tag taxonomy", "tag routing from profile to plugin operations",
                "compilation of OSCAL rules into grants, budgets and OpenFlow policy", "the CMS and its control behaviours",
40→                "Web3 index and on-chain anchoring", "wallet bound to the identity", "trace and vitals UI",
                "deploying the execution tracker that records every tool call", "a dedicated low-privilege identity for the demo",
                "two-approval mechanism for human root actions"],
    "open_issues": ["no Meta API key on the host yet; Muse Spark is reachable only through the founder's IDE agent",
                    "the current model did not make tool calls reliably and retrieval answers came back empty",
                    "live state reads through the identity's filesystem return I/O errors; operations work",
                    "the next release will fail activation until a service health check is fixed",
                    "the UI build in use is a temporary overlay lost on reboot or release",
                    "provisioning new identities is blocked until the storage service is repaired",
                    "this week the platform lost uncommitted work once and two deploys failed"],
50→    "demo_identity": "The identity used for the demo is also the control-plane root identity and holds root grants on the real system.",
    "fallback": "The plan says to record a full run and switch to it if a live dependency fails; no recording exists yet.",
    "business": {
        "wedge": "compliant-by-construction CMS for small regulated businesses, e.g. a Fort Lauderdale firm needing a client portal",
        "parts": ["verifiable autonomous agents", "compliance by construction from OSCAL", "Web3 trust layer for on-chain artifacts"],
        "revenue_model": "not yet stated",
        "first_customer": "not yet named",
    },
}

60→Q = {}
def noul(qid, text, true=None, false=None):
    q = {"type": "noul", "instructions": text}
    if true or false:
        q["criteria"] = {"true": true, "false": false}
    Q[qid] = q

def score(qid, text, levels):
    # Levels are ordered lowest to highest; the API takes them as a list.
    Q[qid] = {"type": "score", "instructions": text, "criteria": list(levels.values())}
70→
# --- judges and pitch
noul("judge.thesis_clear", "Could a non-specialist understand `thesis` after reading it once?")
noul("judge.meta_essential", "Does a step in `golden_path` require Meta's model to work?",
     "a step depends on the model's reasoning or tool use", "every step would work without any language model")
noul("judge.proof_checkable", "Does `golden_path` let a judge check evidence themselves rather than take the presenter's word?")
noul("judge.concept_overload", "Does `pitch_concepts` contain more ideas than a judge can follow in a three-minute demo?")
noul("judge.memorable_moment", "Does `golden_path` contain a moment a judge would likely remember the next day?")
score("judge.overall_appeal", "How compelling is this project to hackathon judges, based on `thesis` and `golden_path`?", {
    "weak": "A judge would see it as a familiar chatbot or infrastructure demo",
80→    "moderate": "A judge would find it interesting but not stand-out",
    "strong": "A judge would see it as novel and clearly demonstrated",
})
# --- feasibility and delivery risk
noul("feas.path_mostly_proven", "Are most steps in `golden_path` already listed in `proven`?")
noul("feas.path_depends_on_open_issue", "Does any step in `golden_path` depend on an item in `open_issues`?")
noul("feas.meta_blocker", "Is wiring Meta's model into the system still unresolved according to `open_issues`?")
noul("feas.tool_calling_risk", "Do `open_issues` show a risk that the model will not make the tool calls the demo needs?")
noul("feas.platform_unstable", "Do `open_issues` describe an unstable platform for a live demo?")
noul("feas.fallback_ready", "Does `fallback` describe a fallback that is ready to use today?",
90→     "a recording or backup exists now", "the fallback is only planned")
score("feas.scope_fit", "How well does the work in `planned` fit ten days for one person with an AI coding agent?", {
    "fits": "The planned work is comfortably achievable in ten days",
    "tight": "The planned work is achievable only if nothing goes wrong",
    "overscoped": "The planned work clearly exceeds ten days for one person",
})
# --- security and authority
noul("sec.demo_overprivileged", "Does `demo_identity` hold more authority than a public demo needs?")
noul("sec.dedicated_identity_planned", "Is a separate low-privilege identity for the demo listed in `planned`?")
noul("sec.receipts_proven", "Is producing a receipt for each operation listed in `proven`?")
100→noul("sec.anchoring_proven", "Is on-chain anchoring listed in `proven`?",
     "anchoring has been demonstrated", "anchoring is only planned")
noul("sec.egress_isolated", "Does `proven` state that the identity cannot reach the backend over the network?")
# --- business and YC
noul("biz.first_customer_named", "Does `business.first_customer` name a specific customer?",
     "a named company or person", "no customer is named")
noul("biz.revenue_stated", "Does `business.revenue_model` describe how the business makes money?")
noul("biz.single_product", "Do the items in `business.parts` describe one product rather than several separate businesses?")
noul("biz.wedge_specific", "Does `business.wedge` describe a specific kind of customer with a specific need?")
noul("biz.web3_may_deter_enterprise", "Would describing the product with a Web3 trust layer make some small-business or enterprise buyers less interested?")
110→
# --- decisions (code, not Jev): finding text when an answer lands on the risky side
RULES = [
    ("judge.thesis_clear", "low", "Rewrite the thesis in plain words for non-specialists."),
    ("judge.meta_essential", "low", "Make Meta's model do a step the demo cannot do without it."),
    ("judge.proof_checkable", "low", "Add a moment where a judge verifies a receipt themselves."),
    ("judge.concept_overload", "high", "Cut the concepts shown in the demo to the three that carry the thesis."),
    ("judge.memorable_moment", "low", "Design one memorable moment (e.g. live redaction or a live refusal)."),
    ("feas.path_mostly_proven", "low", "Most of the golden path is unproven: prove it end to end before adding scope."),
    ("feas.path_depends_on_open_issue", "high", "The golden path depends on open issues: fix those first."),
120→    ("feas.meta_blocker", "high", "Get Meta's model wired in first; it is a hard requirement."),
    ("feas.tool_calling_risk", "high", "De-risk tool calling: test it early with Meta's model or move tool calls into code."),
    ("feas.platform_unstable", "high", "Stabilise the platform: commit often, fix the activation health check, make the UI part of a release."),
    ("feas.fallback_ready", "low", "Record a full fallback run as soon as the golden path first works."),
    ("sec.demo_overprivileged", "high", "Do not demo with root: use a dedicated low-privilege identity or restrict the demo to pre-tested operations."),
    ("sec.anchoring_proven", "low", "Prove on-chain anchoring early; it is the verification claim."),
    ("biz.first_customer_named", "low", "Name a first customer (even a design partner) for the pitch and YC."),
    ("biz.revenue_stated", "low", "State a revenue model for YC."),
    ("biz.single_product", "low", "Present one product; position the other parts as how it works, not separate offerings."),
    ("biz.web3_may_deter_enterprise", "high", "Lead with verifiability and compliance; present the blockchain as the neutral witness, not the product."),
130→]

def read(answers, qid):
    a = answers.get(qid, {})
    return a.get("probability", a.get("noul", a.get("value")))

def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"model": "jev-latest", "state": STATE, "questions": Q}
    (OUT / "request.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
140→    if "--send" not in sys.argv:
        print(f"wrote {OUT/'request.json'} with {len(Q)} questions"); return
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone", data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['TYPESAFE_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:
        body = json.loads(r.read())
    (OUT / "response.json").write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2)[:4000])

if __name__ == "__main__":
150→    main()

noul("biz.revenue_stated", "Does `business.revenue_model` describe how the business makes money?")
noul("biz.single_product", "Do the items in `business.parts` describe one product rather than several separate businesses?")
noul("biz.wedge_specific", "Does `business.wedge` describe a specific kind of customer with a specific need?")
noul("biz.web3_may_deter_enterprise", "Would describing the product with a Web3 trust layer make some small-business or enterprise buyers less interested?")

# --- decisions (code, not Jev): finding text when an answer lands on the risky side
RULES = [
    ("judge.thesis_clear", "low", "Rewrite the thesis in plain words for non-specialists."),
    ("judge.meta_essential", "low", "Make Meta's model do a step the demo cannot do without it."),
    ("judge.proof_checkable", "low", "Add a moment where a judge verifies a receipt themselves."),
    ("judge.concept_overload", "high", "Cut the concepts shown in the demo to the three that carry the thesis."),
    ("judge.memorable_moment", "low", "Design one memorable moment (e.g. live redaction or a live refusal)."),
    ("feas.path_mostly_proven", "low", "Most of the golden path is unproven: prove it end to end before adding scope."),
    ("feas.path_depends_on_open_issue", "high", "The golden path depends on open issues: fix those first."),
    ("feas.meta_blocker", "high", "Get Meta's model wired in first; it is a hard requirement."),
    ("feas.tool_calling_risk", "high", "De-risk tool calling: test it early with Meta's model or move tool calls into code."),
    ("feas.platform_unstable", "high", "Stabilise the platform: commit often, fix the activation health check, make the UI part of a release."),
    ("feas.fallback_ready", "low", "Record a full fallback run as soon as the golden path first works."),
    ("sec.demo_overprivileged", "high", "Do not demo with root: use a dedicated low-privilege identity or restrict the demo to pre-tested operations."),
    ("sec.anchoring_proven", "low", "Prove on-chain anchoring early; it is the verification claim."),
    ("biz.first_customer_named", "low", "Name a first customer (even a design partner) for the pitch and YC."),
    ("biz.revenue_stated", "low", "State a revenue model for YC."),
    ("biz.single_product", "low", "Present one product; position the other parts as how it works, not separate offerings."),
    ("biz.web3_may_deter_enterprise", "high", "Lead with verifiability and compliance; present the blockchain as the neutral witness, not the product."),
]

def read(answers, qid):
    a = answers.get(qid, {})
    return a.get("probability", a.get("noul", a.get("value")))

def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"model": "jev-latest", "state": STATE, "questions": Q}
    (OUT / "request.json").write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
    if "--send" not in sys.argv:
        print(f"wrote {OUT/'request.json'} with {len(Q)} questions"); return
    req = urllib.request.Request("https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone", data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['TYPESAFE_API_KEY']}", "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as r:
        body = json.loads(r.read())
    (OUT / "response.json").write_text(json.dumps(body, indent=2))
    print(json.dumps(body, indent=2)[:4000])

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# System One

> Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as the
questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response also includes
the model used and token usage.



## OpenAPI

````yaml https://api.typesafe.ai/openapi.json post /v1/systemone
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: TypeSafe
  description: >-
    Ask yes/no questions, evaluate statements, select choices, or assign ratings
    to your content. Send your API key in the Authorization header as `Bearer
    <API_KEY>`. Use GET /v1/models to discover available model names.
  version: 0.2.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.typesafe.ai
security: []
paths:
  /v1/systemone:
    post:
      summary: System One
      description: >-
        Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.


        You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as
        the

        questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response
        also includes

        the model used and token usage.
      operationId: systemone_v1_systemone_post
      parameters:
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use assets or box questions.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use long context.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
            examples:
              noul:
                summary: Noul
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    billing:
                      type: noul
                      instructions: Is this message about billing?
              choice:
                summary: Choice
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    tone:
                      type: choice
                      instructions: What is the tone of this message?
                      criteria:
                        angry: An upset or hostile message
                        calm: A neutral or polite message
                        excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
              score:
                summary: Score
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    urgency:
                      type: score
                      instructions: How urgent is this message?
                      criteria:
                        - Can wait
                        - Needs attention this week
                        - Needs attention today
              box:
                summary: 'Box (requires TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true)'
                value:
                  model: jev-preview
                  state: photo
                  questions:
                    red_rectangle:
                      type: box
                      instructions: Locate the red rectangle.
                  assets:
                    photo:
                      type: image
                      format: png
                      data_base64: >-
                        iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAHElEQVR4nGP4TyJgoKcGBgbsaFQDfTUQB4aDBgDAen2fpitsVAAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              description: >-
                The JSON request as the first part, named request, then each
                image as its own part. Every image part needs a unique,
                non-empty name and must be used by exactly one asset's part.
              properties:
                request:
                  description: The JSON request, as the first part.
                  contentMediaType: application/json
                  contentSchema:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
              required:
                - request
              additionalProperties:
                type: string
                description: An image, named by the asset part that uses it.
                contentMediaType: image/*
            encoding:
              request:
                contentType: application/json
        required: true
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Successful Response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneResponse'
              examples:
                noul:
                  summary: Noul
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      billing:
                        type: noul
                        noul: 0.98
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                choice:
                  summary: Choice
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      tone:
                        type: choice
                        choice: calm
                        confidence: 0.7
                        probabilities:
                          angry: 0.15
                          calm: 0.8
                          excited: 0.05
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                score:
                  summary: Score
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      urgency:
                        type: score
                        score: 1.7
                        confidence: 0.55
                        legend:
                          '0': Can wait
                          '1': Needs attention this week
                          '2': Needs attention today
                        probabilities:
                          '0': 0.1
                          '1': 0.1
                          '2': 0.8
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                box:
                  summary: Box
                  value:
                    model: jev-preview
                    answers:
                      red_rectangle:
                        type: box
                        box:
                          top: 0.2
                          bottom: 0.66
                          left: 0.19
                          right: 0.68
                        confidence: null
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 285
                      output_tokens: 20
        '400':
          description: Bad Request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/HTTPBadRequestError'
        '422':
          description: Validation Error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/HTTPValidationError'
      security:
        - HTTPBearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    SystemOneRequest:
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
          title: Model
          description: >-
            Name or alias of the model to use. Available names are returned by
            GET /v1/models.
          examples:
            - jev-latest
        state:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: State
          description: The content all questions in this request refer to.
          examples:
            - I was charged twice. Please help.
            - message: Please help.
              subject: Duplicate charge
        questions:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Question'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Questions
          description: >-
            Questions to ask about the content, each with a name you choose. The
            response uses those names to identify the answers.
          examples:
            - billing:
                instructions: Is this message about billing?
                type: noul
        assets:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Asset'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Assets
          description: >-
            Media assets keyed by an opaque placeholder (recommend a per-image
            UUID). Each placeholder, wherever it appears as or inside a string
            in state, question instructions, or criteria, is replaced with the
            asset. Image assets require a vision-language model.
      type: object
      required:
        - model
        - state
        - questions
      title: SystemOneRequest
      description: Content and named questions to evaluate together using a TypeSafe model.
    SystemOneResponse:
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
          title: Model
          description: >-
            Name of the model that answered the questions. May differ from the
            alias supplied in the request.
          examples:
            - jev-latest
        answers:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Answer'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Answers
          description: >-
            Answers keyed by the question names supplied in the request. Each
            answer's type matches its question's type.
          examples:
            - billing:
                noul: 0.98
                type: noul
        usage:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Usage'
          description: Input and output token counts for this evaluation.
          examples:
            - input_tokens: 120
              output_tokens: 12
      type: object
      required:
        - model
        - answers
        - usage
      title: SystemOneResponse
      description: Answers grouped by question name, with the model used and token usage.
    HTTPBadRequestError:
      type: object
      title: HTTPBadRequestError
      required:
        - detail
      description: Application validation failures returned with HTTP status 400.
      properties:
        detail:
          title: Detail
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
          description: >-
            Explanation of the invalid request. String details and message
            fields are bounded, with shortened text ending with ….
    HTTPValidationError:
      properties:
        detail:
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationError'
          type: array
          title: Detail
          description: >-
            Validation errors describing which request values are missing or
            invalid.
          examples:
            - - loc:
                  - body
                  - state
                msg: Field required
                type: missing
      type: object
      title: HTTPValidationError
      description: Request validation failures returned with HTTP status 422.
    Question:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulQuestion'
          title: Noul
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceQuestion'
          title: Choice
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScoreQuestion'
          title: Score
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxQuestion'
          title: Box
      discriminator:
        propertyName: type
        mapping:
          noul: '#/components/schemas/NoulQuestion'
          choice: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceQuestion'
          score: '#/components/schemas/ScoreQuestion'
          box: '#/components/schemas/BoxQuestion'
      description: A question about the supplied content.
    Asset:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: image
          title: Type
          description: Identifies an image asset.
        format:
          type: string
          enum:
            - png
            - jpg
            - jpeg
          title: Format
          description: >-
            The image format, required with data_base64. The actual format is
            detected from the bytes.
        data_base64:
          type: string
          title: Data Base64
          description: Base64-encoded image data.
        part:
          type: string
          title: Part
          description: >-
            In a multipart request, the name of the image part this asset uses.
            With part, data_base64 is ignored.
      type: object
      title: Asset
      description: >-
        An image that replaces its placeholder: its bytes in data_base64 with
        their format, or, in a multipart request, the name of the image part
        that holds them. Requests with images must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    Answer:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulAnswer'
          title: Noul
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceAnswer'
          title: Choice
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScoreAnswer'
          title: Score
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxAnswer'
          title: Box
      discriminator:
        propertyName: type
        mapping:
          noul: '#/components/schemas/NoulAnswer'
          choice: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceAnswer'
          score: '#/components/schemas/ScoreAnswer'
          box: '#/components/schemas/BoxAnswer'
      description: An answer whose type matches the corresponding question.
    Usage:
      properties:
        input_tokens:
          type: integer
          title: Input Tokens
          description: Number of billable input tokens used to evaluate the request.
          examples:
            - 120
        output_tokens:
          type: integer
          title: Output Tokens
          description: >-
            Number of output tokens used to answer the questions. Output tokens
            are currently free of charge.
          examples:
            - 12
      type: object
      required:
        - input_tokens
        - output_tokens
      title: Usage
      description: Token usage for the request.
    ValidationError:
      properties:
        loc:
          items:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - type: integer
          type: array
          title: Location
          description: >-
            Path to the invalid value: the request location followed by field
            names and array indices. May be empty.
          examples:
            - - body
              - questions
              - urgency
              - score
              - criteria
        msg:
          type: string
          title: Message
          description: >-
            Human-readable explanation of the validation failure. May be
            shortened with ….
          examples:
            - Field required
        type:
          type: string
          title: Error Type
          description: Machine-readable validation error code.
          examples:
            - missing
        input:
          type: string
          title: Input
          description: Text preview of the rejected input. May be shortened with ….
          examples:
            - '{"type":"score"}'
        ctx:
          type: object
          title: Context
          description: >-
            Additional context used to explain the validation failure. Entries
            may be omitted or shortened.
          examples:
            - min_length: 1
      type: object
      required:
        - loc
        - msg
        - type
      title: ValidationError
      description: A request validation error at a specific field or array element.
    NoulQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no question or statement.
          examples:
            - noul
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: The yes/no question or statement to evaluate.
          examples:
            - Is this message spam?
            - This message contains unsolicited advertising.
            - task: Identify unsolicited advertising.
        criteria:
          anyOf:
            - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulCriteria'
            - type: 'null'
          description: Criteria clarifying what counts as a yes or no answer.
          examples:
            - 'false': A legitimate conversation
              'true': Unsolicited advertising
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: NoulQuestion
      description: >-
        A yes/no question or statement, answered with the probability of yes or
        true.
    ChoiceQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a question that selects one of the choices in criteria.
          examples:
            - choice
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What the model should decide when choosing an option.
          examples:
            - What is the tone of this message?
        criteria:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
              - type: 'null'
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          maxProperties: 255
          title: Criteria
          description: >-
            Choice names and descriptions of when each applies. A choice without
            a description is interpreted by its name alone.
          examples:
            - angry: An upset or hostile message
              calm: A neutral or polite message
              excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - criteria
      title: ChoiceQuestion
      description: A question that selects one option from the choices you define.
    ScoreQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: >-
            Identifies a question that rates the content using the levels in
            criteria.
          examples:
            - score
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What the model should rate.
          examples:
            - How urgent is this message?
        criteria:
          items:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          maxItems: 10
          title: Criteria
          description: >-
            Ordered descriptions of the score levels. Each description's
            position determines its score, starting at zero.
          examples:
            - - Can wait
              - Needs attention this week
              - Needs attention today
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - criteria
      title: ScoreQuestion
      description: A question that assigns a score using an ordered rubric.
    BoxQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box question.
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What to locate in the image.
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: BoxQuestion
      description: >-
        A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's
        image. Requests with box questions must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    NoulAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no answer.
          examples:
            - noul
        noul:
          type: number
          title: Noul
          description: >-
            Probability of a yes answer or a true statement, from 0 to 1. Values
            near 1 favor yes or true, values near 0 favor no or false, and
            values near 0.5 indicate uncertainty.
          examples:
            - 0.98
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - noul
      title: NoulAnswer
      description: The probability of a yes answer or a true statement.
    ChoiceAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a selection from the requested choices.
          examples:
            - choice
        choice:
          type: string
          title: Choice
          description: >-
            The name of the choice with the highest probability among the
            question's criteria.
          examples:
            - angry
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the selected choice, from 0 to 1. Higher values
            indicate greater certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain
            selections for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each choice in criteria, keyed by choice name, from 0
            to 1. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - angry: 0.8
              calm: 0.1
              excited: 0.1
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - choice
        - confidence
        - probabilities
      title: ChoiceAnswer
      description: >-
        The selected choice, confidence, and probabilities for a choice
        question.
    ScoreAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a rating against the requested score levels.
          examples:
            - score
        score:
          type: number
          title: Score
          description: >-
            Expected score: the probability-weighted average of the rubric
            levels. May fall between integer levels.
          examples:
            - 1.7
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the score, from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate greater
            certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain ratings for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        legend:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          title: Legend
          description: >-
            The requested criteria mapped to their score levels, so you can
            interpret the score.
          examples:
            - '0': Can wait
              '1': Needs attention this week
              '2': Needs attention today
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each score level, from 0 to 1, using the same keys as
            legend. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score
        - confidence
        - legend
        - probabilities
      title: ScoreAnswer
      description: >-
        An expected score with its rubric, confidence, and score-level
        probabilities.
    BoxAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box answer.
          examples:
            - box
        box:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxCoordinates'
          description: >-
            The box's edges as fractions of image height and width, from 0 to 1.
            Each coordinate is the expected value of its edge's predicted
            position.
          examples:
            - bottom: 0.66
              left: 0.19
              right: 0.68
              top: 0.2
        confidence:
          anyOf:
            - type: number
            - type: 'null'
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence for the given box, from 0 to 1, with 1 being more
            confident. Null when the model does not provide confidence.
          examples:
            - null
            - 0.9
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - box
        - confidence
      title: BoxAnswer
      description: A located box with normalized edge coordinates and confidence.
    NoulCriteria:
      properties:
        'true':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'True'
          description: What counts as a yes answer.
          examples:
            - The message is unsolicited advertising.
        'false':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'False'
          description: What counts as a no answer.
          examples:
            - The message is a legitimate conversation.
      type: object
      title: NoulCriteria
      description: Criteria defining what counts as a yes or no answer.
    BoxCoordinates:
      properties:

# System One

> Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as the
questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response also includes
the model used and token usage.

        probabilities:

## Agent operating contract

### Scope and execution
- Identify the requested outcome, affected components, and evidence needed
70→  to show completion before editing.
- Maintain one shared task with clear file ownership when delegating.
  Subagents inherit the same scope and permission limits.
- Complete authorized work autonomously. Do not ask permission for routine
  reads, isolated tests, reversible edits, or implementation choices.
- Follow demonstrated dependencies. Do not expand a repair into unrelated
  refactoring, new infrastructure, or speculative optimization.
- When new evidence expands the scope, state why and update the task.

### Identity, permissions, and grants
80→- Use the identity and supported control-plane entry point assigned to
  the task. Preserve caller identity through delegated work.
- Existing authorization persists; do not ask for the same approval twice.
- A denied operation is evidence of a permission boundary. Record the
  operation, caller, exact missing capability or policy, and error.
- Do not bypass a denial through another identity, direct database edits,
  alternate transports, or privileged host commands.
- Do not broaden grants, weaken autonomy/security policies, expose secrets,
  or change unrelated identities to make a task pass.
- If a permission change is necessary, first prepare the smallest concrete
90→  change: affected principal, capability, resource scope, duration, expected
  effect, verification, and rollback. Request approval only for the part
  not already explicitly authorized.

### Evidence and verification
- Distinguish proposed, implemented, tested, and deployed work.
- Verify the complete affected workflow, including failure and cancellation
  paths where relevant. A successful component test is not end-to-end proof.
- Use disposable fixtures and bounded workloads. Preserve authoritative
  data and unrelated work.
100→- Report failed or unavailable checks honestly. Do not convert missing
  coverage into a pass or repeatedly run unchanged failing checks.
- Prefer the smallest evidence-backed fix. Add technology only when a
  measured problem justifies its complexity.

### Shared memory and handoff
- Sync decisions, conversations, and tool results to the shared repository
  with agent identity, timestamps, task ID, and source references.
- Use NotebookLM to recover context. Verify current code, permissions,
  configuration, and deployment state against their authoritative sources.
110→- Record the current commit, modified files, validation results, unresolved
  blockers, and exact next action. Update stale conclusions explicitly.
- Never describe planned work or another agent's claim as completed work.

### Completion
- Finish with the outcome, changes, verification, remaining limitations,
  and deployment status.
- Stop when the requested outcome is verified; do not continue into
  speculative optimization or unrelated cleanup.

120→
### Memory routing and authority
- Maintain a map of each memory source: its purpose, scope, owner, and
  how to retrieve and update it.
- Retrieve relevant prior decisions before repeating an investigation
  or proposing an architectural change.
- Treat conversations and tool histories as evidence of prior work.
  Verify present code, deployment, permissions, and runtime state at
  their authoritative sources.
- When sources conflict, identify the disagreement, compare dates and
130→  provenance, and verify the affected claim. Do not silently pick one.
- Write findings back to the appropriate context with source links,
  verification status, and uncertainty. Mark superseded conclusions.
- Store secrets only in the designated secret store, never in general
  conversation memory.

## Host-service policy (runit)

This server runs **Artix Linux with glibc**, not Chimera or a musl-based host.
Build and test the server for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. An installed musl
140→cross target or the Codex executable's own musl packaging does not change the
repository's native target. Any separate container portability test must name
its target and must not substitute for the Artix/glibc verification gate.

This host runs **runit** as PID 1. Manage services with `sudo sv <command> <service>` (e.g., `sudo sv restart op-grpc-bridge`). `sv` needs root to read `supervise/ok`.

- `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run` is the service definition.
- Enabled by a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`.
- Update path: edit the `run` script or install a new binary, then `sudo sv restart <service>`.

150→Do not edit `/run/runit/service` directly. Do not invoke `runsv`/`runsvdir` by hand. **s6 is legacy**: `service6`, `s6-rc`, `s6-*`, `/run/service` are stale — treat any doc assuming them as historical. Note: `/usr/local/bin/systemctl` on this host is a shim that returns plausible answers — using it masks the deprecation; always use `sv`. Do not use `systemctl` or other foreign service-manager CLIs. Container/app deployment uses D-Bus via `busctl`.

## Network

Network topology, Xray policy, decoy/WARP transport and network-critical
service rules are in `docs/src/operations/network.md`. Read it before any
network work; it is not needed otherwise.


**Owner clarification (2026-09-13): there is no deployment script. Deployment
160→is btrfs send/receive of the prepared filesystem snapshot.** The release
boundary is the snapshot's contents and the send/receive transfer. Existing
`deploy/` scripts are source/history or preparation tooling; neither
`build-golden.sh` nor `btrfs-layout.sh` defines the current deployment mechanism.
Never hand-copy binaries onto a running host as a deploy step.

170→live read-only overlay swap at `/opt/op-dbus/current` (active + previous only;

rule above is superseded for this entry point; the transport is still send/receive.

`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` only populates and validates

create the read-only release snapshot, send
or receive it, activate a received filesystem, install files into the running
180→host, or restart services. `--golden-only` remains a compatibility alias for
its default behavior; the former `--live-only` and `--no-restart` modes are

deliberate target service action are separate operator steps.

```sh
CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm            # explicitly reseal after the build
sudo target/release/opblob persist             # retain the catalog across reboot
```

For isolated release preparation, use `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` and pass that catalog as `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; publishing live SHM remains part of activation. Match the service's schema-shaping environment. The renamed cognitive code reads `COGNITIVE_*`: `COGNITIVE_QDRANT_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:6334`, matching the current `deploy/runit/op-grpc-bridge/run`; the historical `COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL=http://10.200.0.2:6334` instruction is obsolete. The commands above describe build/catalog preparation, not deployment. Do not
infer a live install or restart from a successful build or snapshot preparation.

**Clean-baseline activation (2026-09-22):** local releases are received under

`tched-router` runit service owns the pinned threetched executable on loopback

previously missing activation contract, not a new deployment script.

## Workspace shape and build

The workspace has **37 member crates under `crates/`, plus the root `op-dbus`
package** (38 workspace packages total). The root package has no application
210→binary. Binary targets live in members: for example `op-grpc-bridge` and

`op-runit-systemctl`. A binary target or runit directory is source inventory,
not proof that it is deployed; reconcile it with `enabled-services` and
`retired-services`. There is no `op-projection` crate. `[patch.crates-io]`
patches only `rovs-openflow` (vendored fork for OF1.5 `packet_type` match at
`vendor/rovs-openflow`). `op-ml`, `op-gallery-gen`, and `op-uds-relay` have manifests under `crates/`

**Rust-first: no new Python.** New automation, probes, and helpers go in Rust (`cargo run --bin <name> -p <crate> -- <args>`, a small binary in the relevant crate, or a `cargo-script`-style one-shot) or in shell + POSIX tools (`jq`, `curl`, `busctl`, `sv`). All cargo commands run from repo root:

```bash
# Build and deploy at op-web's root (from the UI repo)
cd /srv/git/3tched.com && LANDING=prod VITE_OPDBUS_DOOR=https://10.0.0.2:8090 npm run publish:op-web

execution or repair a pre-installation/deployment gate. Further testing waits

scope. Keep bounded operation receipts, safety checks and readiness evidence
