1→#!/bin/sh
# activate-golden.sh — the one command for deploying a new version.
#
#   sudo ./activate-golden.sh
#
# Run it after the release build and seal:
#   CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
#   sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm && sudo target/release/opblob persist
# OP_RELEASE_DIR selects one prepared optimized artifact directory for both
10→# release-controller verification and golden preparation (default target/release).
#
# What it does:
# 1. Native provision-slots reconciles any interrupted transaction and prepares
#    the owned golden/slot layout. Recovery-only work stops this invocation.
# 2. Prepares /opt/op-dbus/golden from target/release and the sealed catalog
#    (internal helper deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh; it never builds or seals).
# 3. Native release sends/receives the immutable generation into the inactive
#    slot, rotates read-only overlays at the inventory's owned host targets,
#    and restores affected consumers' wanted states. Only active + previous remain.
20→#
# Undo the last release:
#   sudo /usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release-launch rollback
set -eu
PATH=/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
LC_ALL=C
export PATH LC_ALL

REPO=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$(readlink -f "$0")")" && pwd)
OP_RELEASE_DIR=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_RELEASE_DIR:-"$REPO/target/release"}")
30→export OP_RELEASE_DIR
RELEASE_BASE=/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release
RELEASE_LAUNCH=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release-launch
RELEASE_BIN=$RELEASE_BASE/op-release
RELEASE_BOOT=/etc/init.d/op-release-activate

[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: run as root (sudo ./activate-golden.sh)' >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$#" = 0 ] || { echo 'activate-golden.sh: takes no arguments' >&2; exit 1; }
# Check the execution path before invoking any installed kit code. The launcher
# independently checks the complete approved manifest and kernel/BTF pair.
40→for directory in / /usr /usr/local /usr/local/libexec "$RELEASE_BASE" /etc /etc/init.d; do
    directory_mode=0$(stat -c %a "$directory")
    [ -d "$directory" ] && [ ! -L "$directory" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$directory")" = 0:0 ] &&
        [ "$((directory_mode & 07022))" -eq 0 ] ||
        { echo "activate-golden.sh: insecure release-kit directory: $directory" >&2; exit 1; }
done
for artifact in "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$RELEASE_BIN" "$RELEASE_BOOT"; do
    [ -f "$artifact" ] && [ ! -L "$artifact" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a:%h "$artifact")" = 0:0:755:1 ] ||
50→        { echo "activate-golden.sh: install the approved root-owned release kit: $artifact" >&2; exit 1; }
done
cmp -s "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-launch" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BIN" "$OP_RELEASE_DIR/op-release" &&
    cmp -s "$RELEASE_BOOT" "$REPO/deploy/release/op-release-activate" ||
    { echo 'activate-golden.sh: installed release kit differs from this build; refusing an old or mixed kit' >&2; exit 1; }

"$RELEASE_LAUNCH" provision-slots
"$REPO/deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh"
exec "$RELEASE_LAUNCH" release

# System One

> Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.

You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as the
questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response also includes
the model used and token usage.

  title: TypeSafe
  description: >-
    Ask yes/no questions, evaluate statements, select choices, or assign ratings
    to your content. Send your API key in the Authorization header as `Bearer
    <API_KEY>`. Use GET /v1/models to discover available model names.
  version: 0.2.0
servers:
  - url: https://api.typesafe.ai
security: []
paths:
  /v1/systemone:
    post:
      summary: System One
      description: >-
        Answer one or more questions about the content supplied in `state`.


        You can mix question types in one request. Answers use the same names as
        the

        questions, so you can match each result to its question. The response
        also includes

        the model used and token usage.
      operationId: systemone_v1_systemone_post
      parameters:
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use assets or box questions.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
        - name: TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context
          in: header
          description: Set to true to use long context.
          schema:
            type: string
            enum:
              - 'true'
          example: 'true'
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
            examples:
              noul:
                summary: Noul
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    billing:
                      type: noul
                      instructions: Is this message about billing?
              choice:
                summary: Choice
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    tone:
                      type: choice
                      instructions: What is the tone of this message?
                      criteria:
                        angry: An upset or hostile message
                        calm: A neutral or polite message
                        excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
              score:
                summary: Score
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    urgency:
                      type: score
                      instructions: How urgent is this message?
                      criteria:
                        - Can wait
                        - Needs attention this week
                        - Needs attention today
              box:
                summary: 'Box (requires TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true)'
                value:
                  model: jev-preview
                  state: photo
                  questions:
                    red_rectangle:
                      type: box
                      instructions: Locate the red rectangle.
                  assets:
                    photo:
                      type: image
                      format: png
                      data_base64: >-
                        iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAHElEQVR4nGP4TyJgoKcGBgbsaFQDfTUQB4aDBgDAen2fpitsVAAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==

            schema:

                image as its own part. Every image part needs a unique,
                non-empty name and must be used by exactly one asset's part.
              properties:

                  description: The JSON request, as the first part.
                  contentMediaType: application/json
                  contentSchema:

              required:

              additionalProperties:

                description: An image, named by the asset part that uses it.
                contentMediaType: image/*
            encoding:

        required: true
      responses:

          description: Successful Response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneResponse'
              examples:

                  summary: Noul
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      billing:
                        type: noul
                        noul: 0.98
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                choice:
                  summary: Choice
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      tone:
                        type: choice
                        choice: calm
                        confidence: 0.7
                        probabilities:
                          angry: 0.15
                          calm: 0.8
                          excited: 0.05
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                score:
                  summary: Score
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      urgency:
                        type: score
                        score: 1.7
                        confidence: 0.55
                        legend:
                          '0': Can wait
                          '1': Needs attention this week
                          '2': Needs attention today
                        probabilities:
                          '0': 0.1
                          '1': 0.1
                          '2': 0.8
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                box:
                  summary: Box
                  value:
                    model: jev-preview
                    answers:
                      red_rectangle:
                        type: box
                        box:
                          top: 0.2
                          bottom: 0.66
                          left: 0.19
                          right: 0.68
                        confidence: null
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 285
                      output_tokens: 20

          description: Bad Request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:

          description: Validation Error

    HTTPBadRequestError:

        - type

        A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's

          const: noul
          title: Type

          examples:
            - noul

            Probability of a yes answer or a true statement, from 0 to 1. Values

      type: object
      required:

        probabilities:

          title: Probabilities

        score:

          title: Score
          description: >-
            Expected score: the probability-weighted average of the rubric
            levels. May fall between integer levels.
          examples:
            - 1.7
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the score, from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate greater
            certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain ratings for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        legend:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true

              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          title: Legend
          description: >-
            The requested criteria mapped to their score levels, so you can
            interpret the score.
          examples:
            - '0': Can wait
              '1': Needs attention this week
              '2': Needs attention today
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each score level, from 0 to 1, using the same keys as
            legend. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score
        - confidence
        - legend
        - probabilities
      title: ScoreAnswer
      description: >-
        An expected score with its rubric, confidence, and score-level
        probabilities.
    BoxAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box answer.
          examples:
            - box
        box:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxCoordinates'
          description: >-
            The box's edges as fractions of image height and width, from 0 to 1.
            Each coordinate is the expected value of its edge's predicted
            position.
          examples:
            - bottom: 0.66
              left: 0.19
              right: 0.68
              top: 0.2
        confidence:
          anyOf:
            - type: number
            - type: 'null'
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence for the given box, from 0 to 1, with 1 being more
            confident. Null when the model does not provide confidence.
          examples:
            - null
            - 0.9
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - box
        - confidence
      title: BoxAnswer
      description: A located box with normalized edge coordinates and confidence.
    NoulCriteria:
      properties:
        'true':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'True'
          description: What counts as a yes answer.
          examples:
            - The message is unsolicited advertising.
        'false':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'False'
          description: What counts as a no answer.
          examples:
            - The message is a legitimate conversation.
      type: object
      title: NoulCriteria
      description: Criteria defining what counts as a yes or no answer.
    BoxCoordinates:
      properties:
        top:
          type: number
          title: Top
          description: >-
            Top edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.2
        bottom:
          type: number
          title: Bottom
          description: >-
            Bottom edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.66
        left:
          type: number
          title: Left
          description: >-
            Left edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.19
        right:
          type: number
          title: Right
          description: >-
            Right edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.68
      type: object
      required:
        - top
        - bottom
        - left
        - right
      title: BoxCoordinates
      description: >-
        Normalized box edges. Vertical coordinates are measured from the top of
        the image; horizontal coordinates are measured from the left.
  securitySchemes:
    HTTPBearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer

            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
            examples:
              noul:
                summary: Noul
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    billing:
                      type: noul
                      instructions: Is this message about billing?
              choice:
                summary: Choice
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    tone:
                      type: choice
                      instructions: What is the tone of this message?
                      criteria:
                        angry: An upset or hostile message
                        calm: A neutral or polite message
                        excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
              score:
                summary: Score
                value:
                  model: jev-latest
                  state: >-
                    I was charged twice for my subscription this month. Please
                    refund the extra charge.
                  questions:
                    urgency:
                      type: score
                      instructions: How urgent is this message?
                      criteria:
                        - Can wait
                        - Needs attention this week
                        - Needs attention today
              box:
                summary: 'Box (requires TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true)'
                value:
                  model: jev-preview
                  state: photo
                  questions:
                    red_rectangle:
                      type: box
                      instructions: Locate the red rectangle.
                  assets:
                    photo:
                      type: image
                      format: png
                      data_base64: >-
                        iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAHElEQVR4nGP4TyJgoKcGBgbsaFQDfTUQB4aDBgDAen2fpitsVAAAAABJRU5ErkJggg==
          multipart/form-data:
            schema:
              type: object
              description: >-
                The JSON request as the first part, named request, then each
                image as its own part. Every image part needs a unique,
                non-empty name and must be used by exactly one asset's part.
              properties:
                request:
                  description: The JSON request, as the first part.
                  contentMediaType: application/json
                  contentSchema:
                    $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneRequest'
              required:
                - request
              additionalProperties:
                type: string
                description: An image, named by the asset part that uses it.
                contentMediaType: image/*
            encoding:
              request:
                contentType: application/json
        required: true
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Successful Response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/SystemOneResponse'
              examples:
                noul:
                  summary: Noul
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      billing:
                        type: noul
                        noul: 0.98
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                choice:
                  summary: Choice
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      tone:
                        type: choice
                        choice: calm
                        confidence: 0.7
                        probabilities:
                          angry: 0.15
                          calm: 0.8
                          excited: 0.05
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                score:
                  summary: Score
                  value:
                    model: jev-latest
                    answers:
                      urgency:
                        type: score
                        score: 1.7
                        confidence: 0.55
                        legend:
                          '0': Can wait
                          '1': Needs attention this week
                          '2': Needs attention today
                        probabilities:
                          '0': 0.1
                          '1': 0.1
                          '2': 0.8
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 120
                      output_tokens: 12
                box:
                  summary: Box
                  value:
                    model: jev-preview
                    answers:
                      red_rectangle:
                        type: box
                        box:
                          top: 0.2
                          bottom: 0.66
                          left: 0.19
                          right: 0.68
                        confidence: null
                    usage:
                      input_tokens: 285
                      output_tokens: 20
        '400':
          description: Bad Request
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/HTTPBadRequestError'
        '422':
          description: Validation Error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/HTTPValidationError'
      security:
        - HTTPBearer: []
components:
  schemas:
    SystemOneRequest:
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
          title: Model
          description: >-
            Name or alias of the model to use. Available names are returned by
            GET /v1/models.
          examples:
            - jev-latest
        state:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: State
          description: The content all questions in this request refer to.
          examples:
            - I was charged twice. Please help.
            - message: Please help.
              subject: Duplicate charge
        questions:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Question'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Questions
          description: >-
            Questions to ask about the content, each with a name you choose. The
            response uses those names to identify the answers.
          examples:
            - billing:
                instructions: Is this message about billing?
                type: noul
        assets:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Asset'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Assets
          description: >-
            Media assets keyed by an opaque placeholder (recommend a per-image
            UUID). Each placeholder, wherever it appears as or inside a string
            in state, question instructions, or criteria, is replaced with the
            asset. Image assets require a vision-language model.
      type: object
      required:
        - model
        - state
        - questions
      title: SystemOneRequest
      description: Content and named questions to evaluate together using a TypeSafe model.
    SystemOneResponse:
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
          title: Model
          description: >-
            Name of the model that answered the questions. May differ from the
            alias supplied in the request.
          examples:
            - jev-latest
        answers:
          additionalProperties:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Answer'
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          title: Answers
          description: >-
            Answers keyed by the question names supplied in the request. Each
            answer's type matches its question's type.
          examples:
            - billing:
                noul: 0.98
                type: noul
        usage:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/Usage'
          description: Input and output token counts for this evaluation.
          examples:
            - input_tokens: 120
              output_tokens: 12
      type: object
      required:
        - model
        - answers
        - usage
      title: SystemOneResponse
      description: Answers grouped by question name, with the model used and token usage.
    HTTPBadRequestError:
      type: object
      title: HTTPBadRequestError
      required:
        - detail
      description: Application validation failures returned with HTTP status 400.
      properties:
        detail:
          title: Detail
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
          description: >-
            Explanation of the invalid request. String details and message
            fields are bounded, with shortened text ending with ….
    HTTPValidationError:
      properties:
        detail:
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationError'
          type: array
          title: Detail
          description: >-
            Validation errors describing which request values are missing or
            invalid.
          examples:
            - - loc:
                  - body
                  - state
                msg: Field required
                type: missing
      type: object
      title: HTTPValidationError
      description: Request validation failures returned with HTTP status 422.
    Question:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulQuestion'
          title: Noul
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceQuestion'
          title: Choice
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScoreQuestion'
          title: Score
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxQuestion'
          title: Box
      discriminator:
        propertyName: type
        mapping:
          noul: '#/components/schemas/NoulQuestion'
          choice: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceQuestion'
          score: '#/components/schemas/ScoreQuestion'
          box: '#/components/schemas/BoxQuestion'
      description: A question about the supplied content.
    Asset:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: image
          title: Type
          description: Identifies an image asset.
        format:
          type: string
          enum:
            - png
            - jpg
            - jpeg
          title: Format
          description: >-
            The image format, required with data_base64. The actual format is
            detected from the bytes.
        data_base64:
          type: string
          title: Data Base64
          description: Base64-encoded image data.
        part:
          type: string
          title: Part
          description: >-
            In a multipart request, the name of the image part this asset uses.
            With part, data_base64 is ignored.
      type: object
      title: Asset
      description: >-
        An image that replaces its placeholder: its bytes in data_base64 with
        their format, or, in a multipart request, the name of the image part
        that holds them. Requests with images must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    Answer:
      oneOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulAnswer'
          title: Noul
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceAnswer'
          title: Choice
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/ScoreAnswer'
          title: Score
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxAnswer'
          title: Box
      discriminator:
        propertyName: type
        mapping:
          noul: '#/components/schemas/NoulAnswer'
          choice: '#/components/schemas/ChoiceAnswer'
          score: '#/components/schemas/ScoreAnswer'
          box: '#/components/schemas/BoxAnswer'
      description: An answer whose type matches the corresponding question.
    Usage:
      properties:
        input_tokens:
          type: integer
          title: Input Tokens
          description: Number of billable input tokens used to evaluate the request.
          examples:
            - 120
        output_tokens:
          type: integer
          title: Output Tokens
          description: >-
            Number of output tokens used to answer the questions. Output tokens
            are currently free of charge.
          examples:
            - 12
      type: object
      required:
        - input_tokens
        - output_tokens
      title: Usage
      description: Token usage for the request.
    ValidationError:
      properties:
        loc:
          items:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - type: integer
          type: array
          title: Location
          description: >-
            Path to the invalid value: the request location followed by field
            names and array indices. May be empty.
          examples:
            - - body
              - questions
              - urgency
              - score
              - criteria
        msg:
          type: string
          title: Message
          description: >-
            Human-readable explanation of the validation failure. May be
            shortened with ….
          examples:
            - Field required
        type:
          type: string
          title: Error Type
          description: Machine-readable validation error code.
          examples:
            - missing
        input:
          type: string
          title: Input
          description: Text preview of the rejected input. May be shortened with ….
          examples:
            - '{"type":"score"}'
        ctx:
          type: object
          title: Context
          description: >-
            Additional context used to explain the validation failure. Entries
            may be omitted or shortened.
          examples:
            - min_length: 1
      type: object
      required:
        - loc
        - msg
        - type
      title: ValidationError
      description: A request validation error at a specific field or array element.
    NoulQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no question or statement.
          examples:
            - noul
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: The yes/no question or statement to evaluate.
          examples:
            - Is this message spam?
            - This message contains unsolicited advertising.
            - task: Identify unsolicited advertising.
        criteria:
          anyOf:
            - $ref: '#/components/schemas/NoulCriteria'
            - type: 'null'
          description: Criteria clarifying what counts as a yes or no answer.
          examples:
            - 'false': A legitimate conversation
              'true': Unsolicited advertising
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: NoulQuestion
      description: >-
        A yes/no question or statement, answered with the probability of yes or
        true.
    ChoiceQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a question that selects one of the choices in criteria.
          examples:
            - choice
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What the model should decide when choosing an option.
          examples:
            - What is the tone of this message?
        criteria:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
              - type: 'null'
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          minProperties: 1
          maxProperties: 255
          title: Criteria
          description: >-
            Choice names and descriptions of when each applies. A choice without
            a description is interpreted by its name alone.
          examples:
            - angry: An upset or hostile message
              calm: A neutral or polite message
              excited: An enthusiastic or eager message
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - criteria
      title: ChoiceQuestion
      description: A question that selects one option from the choices you define.
    ScoreQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: >-
            Identifies a question that rates the content using the levels in
            criteria.
          examples:
            - score
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What the model should rate.
          examples:
            - How urgent is this message?
        criteria:
          items:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          maxItems: 10
          title: Criteria
          description: >-
            Ordered descriptions of the score levels. Each description's
            position determines its score, starting at zero.
          examples:
            - - Can wait
              - Needs attention this week
              - Needs attention today
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - criteria
      title: ScoreQuestion
      description: A question that assigns a score using an ordered rubric.
    BoxQuestion:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box question.
        instructions:
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: Instructions
          description: What to locate in the image.
      type: object
      required:
        - type
      title: BoxQuestion
      description: >-
        A question that locates what its instructions describe in the request's
        image. Requests with box questions must send the header
        TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true.
    NoulAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: noul
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a yes/no answer.
          examples:
            - noul
        noul:
          type: number
          title: Noul
          description: >-
            Probability of a yes answer or a true statement, from 0 to 1. Values
            near 1 favor yes or true, values near 0 favor no or false, and
            values near 0.5 indicate uncertainty.
          examples:
            - 0.98
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - noul
      title: NoulAnswer
      description: The probability of a yes answer or a true statement.
    ChoiceAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: choice
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a selection from the requested choices.
          examples:
            - choice
        choice:
          type: string
          title: Choice
          description: >-
            The name of the choice with the highest probability among the
            question's criteria.
          examples:
            - angry
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the selected choice, from 0 to 1. Higher values
            indicate greater certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain
            selections for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each choice in criteria, keyed by choice name, from 0
            to 1. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - angry: 0.8
              calm: 0.1
              excited: 0.1
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - choice
        - confidence
        - probabilities
      title: ChoiceAnswer
      description: >-
        The selected choice, confidence, and probabilities for a choice
        question.
    ScoreAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: score
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a rating against the requested score levels.
          examples:
            - score
        score:
          type: number
          title: Score
          description: >-
            Expected score: the probability-weighted average of the rubric
            levels. May fall between integer levels.
          examples:
            - 1.7
        confidence:
          type: number
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence in the score, from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate greater
            certainty; use lower values to flag uncertain ratings for review.
          examples:
            - 0.9
        legend:
          additionalProperties:
            anyOf:
              - type: string
              - additionalProperties: true
                type: object
              - items: {}
                type: array
            x-accepts: string | object | array
          type: object
          title: Legend
          description: >-
            The requested criteria mapped to their score levels, so you can
            interpret the score.
          examples:
            - '0': Can wait
              '1': Needs attention this week
              '2': Needs attention today
        probabilities:
          additionalProperties:
            type: number
          type: object
          title: Probabilities
          description: >-
            Probability of each score level, from 0 to 1, using the same keys as
            legend. Shows how likely the alternatives are; values sum to
            approximately 1.
          examples:
            - '0': 0.1
              '1': 0.1
              '2': 0.8
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - score
        - confidence
        - legend
        - probabilities
      title: ScoreAnswer
      description: >-
        An expected score with its rubric, confidence, and score-level
        probabilities.
    BoxAnswer:
      properties:
        type:
          type: string
          const: box
          title: Type
          description: Identifies a box answer.
          examples:
            - box
        box:
          $ref: '#/components/schemas/BoxCoordinates'
          description: >-
            The box's edges as fractions of image height and width, from 0 to 1.
            Each coordinate is the expected value of its edge's predicted
            position.
          examples:
            - bottom: 0.66
              left: 0.19
              right: 0.68
              top: 0.2
        confidence:
          anyOf:
            - type: number
            - type: 'null'
          title: Confidence
          description: >-
            Confidence for the given box, from 0 to 1, with 1 being more
            confident. Null when the model does not provide confidence.
          examples:
            - null
            - 0.9
      type: object
      required:
        - type
        - box
        - confidence
      title: BoxAnswer
      description: A located box with normalized edge coordinates and confidence.
    NoulCriteria:
      properties:
        'true':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'True'
          description: What counts as a yes answer.
          examples:
            - The message is unsolicited advertising.
        'false':
          anyOf:
            - type: string
            - additionalProperties: true
              type: object
            - items: {}
              type: array
            - type: 'null'
          x-accepts: string | object | array
          title: 'False'
          description: What counts as a no answer.
          examples:
            - The message is a legitimate conversation.
      type: object
      title: NoulCriteria
      description: Criteria defining what counts as a yes or no answer.
    BoxCoordinates:
      properties:
        top:
          type: number
          title: Top
          description: >-
            Top edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.2
        bottom:
          type: number
          title: Bottom
          description: >-
            Bottom edge of the box, as a fraction of image height from the top
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.66
        left:
          type: number
          title: Left
          description: >-
            Left edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.19
        right:
          type: number
          title: Right
          description: >-
            Right edge of the box, as a fraction of image width from the left
            (0-1).
          examples:
            - 0.68
      type: object
      required:
        - top
        - bottom
        - left
        - right
      title: BoxCoordinates
      description: >-
        Normalized box edges. Vertical coordinates are measured from the top of
        the image; horizontal coordinates are measured from the left.
  securitySchemes:
    HTTPBearer:
      type: http
      scheme: bearer

````

> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt

# Jev with coding agents

> What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.

If you found TypeSafe while looking for a model to plug into your coding agent, start here. Jev is **not** a drop-in replacement for the LLM behind Claude Code, Cursor, opencode, Copilot, Muse Spark, Grok Bot, or similar tools. Instead, you can use your coding agent as usual to write code that uses Jev to make decisions.

## Jev is not a chat or code-completion LLM

Jev is a [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). It does not generate text, write code, or hold a conversation. It takes a [state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) and a set of typed [questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) and returns structured answers your code can use directly:

* A `choice` from a list of options, with per-option probabilities.
* A `score` on a rubric you define.
* A `noul` (0–1) for a true/false statement.

Coding agents rely on an LLM that streams text, calls tools, and edits files based on natural-language instructions. Jev does none of that. There is no `model: "jev-latest"` setting that turns your coding agent into a Jev-powered agent, because the two systems solve different problems.

## What you probably want instead

Pick the row that matches what you were trying to do:

| You wanted to... | Do this |
| - | - |
| Make your coding agent better at *writing code that uses TypeSafe* | Install the [TypeSafe agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md). It gives Claude Code, Codex, and other agents full context on the Jev API, the [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives), and the [patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) so they can generate correct TypeSafe integrations for you. |
| Use Jev inside an app or agent you're building — for routing, classification, scoring, guardrails, or any structured decision | Start with the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md), then read [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and the [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) for common architectures like [confidence routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/confidence-routing.md) and [intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md). |
| Replace or swap the model that powers a coding agent | Jev isn't the tool for this. Keep using an LLM-based coding agent, and use Jev separately wherever your product needs a fast, calibrated, structured decision. |
| Try Jev before writing any code | Open the [Playground](https://console.typesafe.ai/playground), paste some text as the state, and add a few questions. See the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md) for a walkthrough. |

## When Jev is worth reaching for

Even though Jev isn't a coding-agent LLM, it's often exactly the right tool *inside* an agent or app you're building with a coding agent. Reach for Jev when your code needs to:

* Route a request to one of a fixed set of destinations, and know how confident that routing is.
* Score something on a rubric (urgency, quality, risk) and branch on the number.
* Check whether a statement is true of a document, message, or record before taking an action.
* Replace a fragile prompt that asks an LLM to "return JSON" with a call that returns typed values by construction.

If any of that matches what you're building, the fastest path in is the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md), then the [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) reference for the question types.

## Next steps

* [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) — What a System One model is and how it differs from an LLM.
* [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md) — Try Jev in the Playground, over HTTP, or with the Python SDK.
* [Agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md) — Give your coding agent context on the TypeSafe API.
* [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) — Common architectures for building with TypeSafe.

# Jev with coding agents

> What Jev is (and isn't) when you're using a coding agent.

If you found TypeSafe while looking for a model to plug into your coding agent, start here. Jev is **not** a drop-in replacement for the LLM behind Claude Code, Cursor, opencode, Copilot, Muse Spark, Grok Bot, or similar tools. Instead, you can use your coding agent as usual to write code that uses Jev to make decisions.

## Jev is not a chat or code-completion LLM

Jev is a [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). It does not generate text, write code, or hold a conversation. It takes a [state](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) and a set of typed [questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) and returns structured answers your code can use directly:

* A `choice` from a list of options, with per-option probabilities.
* A `score` on a rubric you define.
* A `noul` (0–1) for a true/false statement.

Coding agents rely on an LLM that streams text, calls tools, and edits files based on natural-language instructions. Jev does none of that. There is no `model: "jev-latest"` setting that turns your coding agent into a Jev-powered agent, because the two systems solve different problems.

## What you probably want instead

Pick the row that matches what you were trying to do:

| You wanted to... | Do this |
| - | - |
| Make your coding agent better at *writing code that uses TypeSafe* | Install the [TypeSafe agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md). It gives Claude Code, Codex, and other agents full context on the Jev API, the [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives), and the [patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) so they can generate correct TypeSafe integrations for you. |
| Use Jev inside an app or agent you're building — for routing, classification, scoring, guardrails, or any structured decision | Start with the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md), then read [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and the [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) for common architectures like [confidence routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/confidence-routing.md) and [intent routing](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/intent-routing.md). |
| Replace or swap the model that powers a coding agent | Jev isn't the tool for this. Keep using an LLM-based coding agent, and use Jev separately wherever your product needs a fast, calibrated, structured decision. |
| Try Jev before writing any code | Open the [Playground](https://console.typesafe.ai/playground), paste some text as the state, and add a few questions. See the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md) for a walkthrough. |

## When Jev is worth reaching for

Even though Jev isn't a coding-agent LLM, it's often exactly the right tool *inside* an agent or app you're building with a coding agent. Reach for Jev when your code needs to:

* Route a request to one of a fixed set of destinations, and know how confident that routing is.
* Score something on a rubric (urgency, quality, risk) and branch on the number.
* Check whether a statement is true of a document, message, or record before taking an action.
* Replace a fragile prompt that asks an LLM to "return JSON" with a call that returns typed values by construction.

If any of that matches what you're building, the fastest path in is the [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md), then the [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives) reference for the question types.

## Next steps

* [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md) — What a System One model is and how it differs from an LLM.
* [Quick start](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/quickstart.md) — Try Jev in the Playground, over HTTP, or with the Python SDK.
* [Agent skill](https://docs.typesafe.ai/agent-skill.md) — Give your coding agent context on the TypeSafe API.
* [Patterns](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns.md) — Common architectures for building with TypeSafe.


This documentation is built and hosted on [Mintlify](https://mintlify.com), a developer documentation platform.

# Models

Jev is TypeSafe's flagship model and the first [System One model](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md). Every model on this page is served by the same endpoint, `POST /v1/systemone`. The request's `model` field selects which one handles it; see the [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) for the full request shape.

## Current models

| | Jev 1.14 | Jev 1.13 |
| :- | :- | :- |
| Model ID | `jev-1.14.0` | `jev-1.13.0` |
| Price (per Btok / per Mtok) | \$42 / \$0.042 | \$42 / \$0.042 |
| Context length | 64k per-request / 32k per-question | 64k per-request / 32k per-question |
| Input | Text | Text |

Jev 1.14 is the newest Jev release, available from October 14, 2026.

* **Price:** You pay per input token. Output tokens are free. A Btok is a billion tokens and an Mtok is a million tokens.
* **Context length:** Two limits, the per-request context and the per-question context. See [Context length](#context-length). To raise both, see [Long context](#long-context).
* **Input:** Jev reads natural-language text, sent as a string, a JSON object, or an array of text values. It does not accept audio or video. Convert those into text or structured fields before you send them as `state`. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md) for the shapes `state` accepts.

## Context length

Jev ingests the `state` once and evaluates every question against it in parallel. A request has to fit two context limits:

* **Per-request context** (`per_request_context`): the `state` plus all questions combined.
* **Per-question context** (`per_question_context`): the `state` plus any one question.

There is no separate limit on the number of questions in a request. Any number of questions is allowed as long as the request fits both limits. See [Speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md) for packing many questions into one request, and [Jev 1.13 jaggedness](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md) for how accuracy shifts as the state grows.

To raise both limits, see [Long context](#long-context).

### Long context

Long context is off by default and works on both Jev 1.14 and Jev 1.13. To turn it on, send the `TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true` header with each request that needs it. With the header, the per-request context and the per-question context are both 262k tokens. Requests without the header keep the default limits in the table above.

```bash theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-latest",
    "state": "<a long contract, transcript, or record>",
    "questions": {
      "has_termination_clause": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the `state` include a clause that lets either party end the agreement early?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

Long context costs the same per token as any other request. It is slower and less accurate than staying within the default limits, so turn it on only for requests that need it.

## Rate limits

Rate limits are set per organization. Your organization's current limits are in the [developer console](https://console.typesafe.ai/rate-limits).

Limits are measured in tokens per second and requests per second. A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our [client SDKs](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk.md) retry these requests by default, waiting longer between each attempt, and follow the `retry-after` header when the response includes one. If you call the HTTP API directly, see [Handling rate limits](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api/errors.md#handling-rate-limits).

Higher limits are available on custom and enterprise plans. To request a higher limit, fill out the [rate limit increase request form](https://support.typesafe.ai/forms/rate-limit-increase-request).

## Aliases

An alias is a model name that points to a versioned model ID. Send it in the `model` field the same way you send a model ID.

| Alias | Points to | Meaning |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `jev-latest` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent stable, official release. The default in our client SDKs, and the name the examples in these docs use. |
| `jev-preview` | `jev-1.14.0` | The most recent release, official or not. Moves ahead of `jev-latest` when a preview build is available. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> `jev-preview` currently points to the same model as `jev-latest`. There is no preview build available right now.

An alias moves when a new release ships, so its answers can change without any change to your code. Each response's `model` field gives the versioned ID that answered, so you can log which model produced each result. If you have tuned confidence thresholds against one version, send that version's ID instead of the alias, and switch to the new version when you are ready.

## Customizing Jev

Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. It is trained with [RLCD](https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction/machine-learning-primer.md) to return calibrated decisions, and the same weights serve every account. You shape its answers to your domain through the request rather than through per-account weights:

* Put your proprietary content, records, and reference material in the `state` field. See [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md).
* Encode your domain rules and boundary cases in the `instructions` and `criteria` of each question. See [How to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) and [Advanced: structure](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/advanced.md).
* Decompose broad judgments into atomic questions and combine the outputs in code. See [Composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and the [AutoResearch cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md) for training a downstream classical model on Jev's probabilities.

## Language support

Jev accepts natural-language text. English is the primary training language and where accuracy is currently best. Other languages, including CJK scripts, are handled but not equally well; test on your own content before relying on Jev for a non-English workload, and pay close attention to [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) when routing.

## Data handling

Jev is not trained on customer requests or responses. See [Legal](https://docs.typesafe.ai/legal.md) for the Data Processing Agreement, the Privacy Policy, and details on zero data retention (ZDR) for enterprise customers.

## Listing models

`GET /v1/models` returns the names your account can send in the `model` field, each with a description and a release date. It currently lists the aliases. Versioned IDs such as `jev-1.14.0` are accepted by the `model` field whether or not they appear in the list.

```bash cURL theme={null}
curl https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: *** $TYPESAFE_API_KEY"
```

```python Python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    for model in client.models.list().models:
        print(model.name, model.release_date, model.description)
```

```typescript JavaScript theme={null}
import { TypeSafeClient } from "@typesafe-ai/sdk";

const client = new TypeSafeClient();
const models = await client.models.list();
for (const model of models) {
  console.log(model.name, model.release_date, model.description);
}
```

**models** `array` *required*

One entry per model or alias.

**properties**

**name** `string` *required*

The model ID or alias, as accepted by the `model` field.

**description** `string` *required*

What the model is for.

**release\_date** `string` *required*

When the model or alias was released.

See the [Python](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python/api/clients/sync.md#typesafe_sdk.Models.list) and [JavaScript](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript/api/interfaces/Models.md) SDK references for the full method signatures.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Request rules and errors

> Request limits, compression, and HTTP status codes

## Request rules

These rules apply to every request:

| Rule | Limit |
| - | - |
| Body size | At most 32 MiB. Headers don't count. |
| Encoding | UTF-8 JSON without a byte order mark (BOM). |
| Nesting | At most 64 nested levels of objects and arrays in each of `state`, `instructions`, and `criteria`. Flatten deeper content. |
| Numbers | Finite numbers only. `NaN`, `Infinity`, and numbers too large to represent, such as `1e400`, are rejected. Send identifiers and exact large quantities as strings. |

A body over 32 MiB returns `413`; the other rules return `400`.

### Compression

You can compress the body with `Content-Encoding: gzip` (or `x-gzip`) or `zstd`. Use one compression layer, and keep zstd's window at most 8 MiB. The 32 MiB limit applies to both the compressed and the decompressed body. An unsupported `Content-Encoding` or more than one layer returns `415`; a malformed compressed body returns `400`.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes with a JSON body describing what went wrong.

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `400 Bad Request` | The body breaks a [request rule](#request-rules), such as invalid UTF-8, too much nesting, a number that isn't finite, or a malformed compressed body. With `max_tokens_exceeded`, the request is longer than the model's [context length](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md). |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Missing or invalid API key. Check the `Authorization` header. |
| `413 Payload Too Large` | The body is over 32 MiB. See [Request rules](#request-rules). |
| `415 Unsupported Media Type` | The body uses an unsupported `Content-Encoding` or more than one compression layer. See [Compression](#compression). |
| `422 Unprocessable Entity` | The request body failed validation, for example a missing required field or a malformed question. The body details the offending field. |
| `429 Too Many Requests` | You have exceeded your rate limit. Back off and retry after a short delay. |
| `529 Overloaded` | TypeSafe is temporarily overloaded. Retry after a short delay. |

## Handling rate limits

When you receive a `429 Too Many Requests` or `529 Overloaded` response, retry the request with exponential backoff instead of retrying immediately. Our client SDKs handle this automatically, so no extra handling is needed if you use one of our SDKs with its default retry policy.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt

# Noul

> A Noul question asks the TypeSafe model to evaluate a yes/no question and return the probability that the answer is yes.

Use a Noul when the answer is yes or no. For example, does this message ask for a refund, does this resume mention distributed systems, does this comment contain personal data. If the answer is one of several options, use a [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md). If it's a position on a spectrum, use a [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md). [Choose a question type](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives#choose-a-question-type) compares all three.

A Noul answer is a single number representing the probability that the answer is yes where 0 means no and 1 means yes.

## Request structure

The POST request body to the [TypeSafe API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) has the same three top-level fields as any other question type: `state`, which is the content to evaluate; `model`; and `questions`. Each Noul question has the following fields:

* `type`: Always `"noul"`.
* `instructions`: The yes/no question the model answers, or a statement for it to judge.
* `criteria`: Optional. An object with `true` and `false` descriptions of what a yes and a no mean.

Below is a request where the state is a support message and the two questions are whether the customer wants a person and whether they have contacted support before:

Try it in the Playground →

You choose the question ids, `is_human_escalation` and `is_repeat_contact` here. The ids are not sent to the model. Each answer is returned under the same id. The first question relies on `instructions` alone. The second adds `criteria` to say what counts as a yes and what counts as a no.

With the [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python.md), the same questions are `Noul` objects:

```python theme={null}
from typesafe_sdk import Noul, NoulCriteria, TypeSafeClient

with TypeSafeClient() as client:
    response = client.system_one(
        model="jev-latest",
        state="I have asked three times now. Can I please just talk to a real person?",
        questions={
            "is_human_escalation": Noul(
                instructions="Is the customer asking for a human agent?",
            ),
            "is_repeat_contact": Noul(
                instructions="Has the customer contacted support about this before?",
                criteria=NoulCriteria(

```python theme={null}

SAME_PERSON = "Is the resume for the same person as `potential_duplicate`?"

    """One Noul per candidate record, all asking the same question."""
    return {
        f"same_as_record_{candidate['id']}": Noul(
            instructions={
                "potential_duplicate": {
                    "name": candidate["name"],
                    "location": candidate["location"],
                    "last_employer": candidate["last_employer"],
                },
                "question": SAME_PERSON,
            },
        )
        for candidate in candidates
    }

            model="jev-latest",
            state={"resume": resume},
            questions=duplicate_questions(candidates),
        )

        question_id
        for question_id, answer in response.answers.items()
        if answer.noul > 0.7
    ]
```

## Noul in the cookbooks

Take a look at our cookbooks to see apps using Noul questions:

* [Parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md) runs a 13-question regulatory checklist over one article in a single request.
* [Self-consistency: nouls](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md) scores an insurance claim against a 15-question rubric and measures how stable the values are across runs.
* [Re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md) uses the probability itself, not a threshold: one Noul per query-candidate pair, then sorts candidates by the value.
* [Line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md) pairs a Choice that finds the matching line with a Noul that checks whether the document contains an answer at all.
* [Structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md) asks one Noul per pair of lines, whether a line break split a sentence, to rebuild paragraphs from plain text.

        )
    return [

        for question_id, answer in response.answers.items()
        if answer.noul > 0.7
    ]

The [structured-data-extraction cascade cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md) uses structured instructions to verify an extracted record. Every field gets the same set of questions. Each question's `instructions` object has the question text in the `main_question` property. There are also `field_spec` and `extracted_field` properties that change for each field.

## Noul in the cookbooks

Take a look at our cookbooks to see apps using Noul questions:

* [Parallel questions](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/parallel_questions.md) runs a 13-question regulatory checklist over one article in a single request.
* [Self-consistency: nouls](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/consistency_noul_cookbook.md) scores an insurance claim against a 15-question rubric and measures how stable the values are across runs.
* [Re-ranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md) uses the probability itself, not a threshold: one Noul per query-candidate pair, then sorts candidates by the value.
* [Line-by-line search](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/semantic_find.md) pairs a Choice that finds the matching line with a Noul that checks whether the document contains an answer at all.
* [Structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md) asks one Noul per pair of lines, whether a line break split a sentence, to rebuild paragraphs from plain text.
