   `docs/src/operations/network.md`). `openflow.write` stays withheld until
   enforcement refuses a flow on any bridge other than `etched0`. Do not put
   the old `hackbr0` NIC back on the root chatbot.

Leave the root chatbot as `3tchedCtlChatbot`, session
`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`. It is the root, not the subsidiary.

## New

New on 2026-10-30, because the sealed identity path cannot assign the key:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Display name | `etched::hackathon` |
| Incus name | `etched-hackathon` (a name cannot contain `::`) |
| State | Stopped. **Proven.** |
| Session | `cc59ab57-d94a-8334-222b-8077ef033320`, Blake3 `derive_session_id` of the new public key |
| Public key | `Wycws7Udq0XTSN7I45JPP+CL9ZS4MxhXlhM4zAn8FX0=` |
| Private key | `/root/etched-hackathon.key` inside the container, mode 600, root. The host copy was removed. |
| Disk | Its own root volume on pool `3tched`. The root chatbot's persist volume is not attached. |
| Profile | `3tched-lungs`, so a later start can see the lungs socket |
| NIC | `eth0`, bridged, parent `etched0` only. Not `ovsbr0`, not `hackbr0`. |
| Sled | Not registered. This container is not yet an identity. |

The container is a wholesale copy of `3tchedCtlChatbot` with the name and
keys changed. It is not a seed provision and it is not a second root.

## Old and existing

These were already on the host. They were not replaced.

| Item | What it still is |
|---|---|
| Root chatbot | `3tchedCtlChatbot`, running, display name `control-plane-chatbot`, session `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, public key `Env5zPMmM1Zhypu5/DY/yU4PRYW/4AOEq2KZ4OSc+18=`, persist volume `3tchedCtlChatbot-persist`. **Proven** still running after the copy. |
| Hackathon mount | `/home/3tched/Hackathon/3tchedfs`, runit `subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs`, Linux user `3tched` (uid 1001). **Proven** mounted. `SESSION=` is still the root session. |
| `etched0` | OVS bridge, fail-mode `secure`, no address, no uplink, no extra ports. Created 2026-10-28 with `ovs-vsctl`, so it has no identity and no receipt. |
| `hackbr0` | The 2026-10-28 internet-only Incus bridge. It is down. Its NIC is not on the root container and not on the clone. |
| Other instances | `3tched-container` and `chatbot-template-sysprep` are stopped. `qdrant-recovered` is running. None of them is the subsidiary. |
| Identity rule | The sled is the identity. Session id is derived from the public key. The bridge verifies storage; it does not compose a root. |

The 2026-10-28 docs said the hackathon subsidiary *was* `3tchedCtlChatbot`.
That sentence described the mount that is still live. It is not the owner
model as of 2026-10-30.

## What changed in the old

Brought forward only far enough for the clone to exist beside the root.
Nothing below re-keyed the root or moved the live mount.

| Old thing | Change on 2026-10-30 |
|---|---|
| `3tchedCtlChatbot` | Copied to `etched-hackathon` with `incus copy --instance-only`. The source was left running, on the same session, with the same public key and the same persist volume. |
| Copy's inherited identity labels | Display name, public key, session id, and `lxc.uts.name` set to the clone. `user.opdbus.creation_digest` and `user.opdbus.creation_operation` unset so the copy does not claim the root's creation receipt. |
| Copy's `persist` device | Removed, so the clone does not mount `3tchedCtlChatbot-persist`. |
| `etched0` | The bridge was not edited. The clone's Incus NIC names it as parent. While the clone is stopped, `etched0` still has no extra ports. |
| Hackathon run script and mount | Unchanged. Calls as `3tched` are still the root chatbot. |
| `docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md`, `docs/RUNTIME.md`, `docs/DEV-CYCLE.md` | The old "the subsidiary is the root container" lines now point here. |
| `docs/src/operations/network.md` | A 2026-10-30 note records the clone NIC. The 2026-10-28 `etched0` and `hackbr0` notes stay as history. |

## Also on the host, not the subsidiary

Stale release-kit copies from 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-23 were removed because
their `op-release` binaries did not match the installed kit. The installed
kit that remains is `/usr/local/libexec/opdbus-release/op-release`,
`op-release-launch`, and `/etc/init.d/op-release-activate`, with
`manifest.sha256` matching those three. Slot B
`release-640f40aa-7b7a-446e-a614-3aecb7771d90` was left mounted. The
unfinished journal at `quiescent-delete:489` for candidate
`release-97d42309-3d63-4227-ac48-23f492466652` was left in `slots.json`.
That journal is not this subsidiary.

Two distinct queues are needed. One is for human review of existing chatbots. The other is for candidates promoted for catalog consideration.

Existing chatbots flagged for review are already in use. Catalog candidates come from chat requests and require human approval to enter the catalog. The current system uses private candidates, suggestions, and an approved catalog.

A backend schema change is blocked by the sealed plugin. The chatbot path can be distinguished without adding fields by using reserved prefixes in titles or prompts. These components would still need to be submitted as suggestions, though suggestions lack a category field.

The SuggestionSummary struct lacks a category field. A title prefix could separate review items from candidates, but the UI would need to parse titles to split them into sections. Using the mode field is risky because ChatMode is a closed enum and adding a new value could break validation. Adding a new plugin field would require a sealed catalog change, so it cannot be live on 8080 until the next golden deploy.

The implementation will live in the existing UI gallery source. The review panel will split into two sections: human review for chatbot components already in use, and catalog candidates for user-saved items awaiting approval. Chatbot-defined components will be saved with a `review:chatbot` marker to separate them from regular suggestions.

Chatbot components are registered in memory so the current page renders, but they remain outside the approved catalog until a human approves them. User-saved chat items become catalog candidates via `saveCandidate` and `suggestCandidate`. Chatbot components stay in their own human review queue.

Both chatbot and user paths call `suggestCandidate`, so they land in the same suggestions list. The UI splits them by a title marker, since no new field can be added to the schema. A prompt prefix was considered but rejected because `SuggestionSummary` does not expose prompt text; only full `Candidate` objects carry it.

Mode is a closed set. I can see the available modes.

A new mode would require a plugin change that only goes live after a rebuild. The UI can still distinguish categories using the prompt field on candidates. I'll embed the category in the suggestion title and display a clean name. The 8080 app is the deployed bundle, so source changes won't update it until rebuilt.

The user wants a clear product behavior.

Merge conflicts block safe edits to the working tree. I will explain the two categories first. Then I will implement the distinction only in clean files or document it if compilation fails.

A new `review-lane.ts` module will tag prompts with `review:human` for active chatbots and `review:catalog` for candidate submissions. `keepRegistered` will mark items for human review. `save()` will mark them as catalog candidates without auto-suggesting.

The human-review lane will hold active chatbot components awaiting a reviewer. Catalog candidates are items chosen from chat that remain in a separate queue until someone explicitly promotes them for consideration.

The gallery panel will show three lanes: human review, catalog candidates, and active catalog. Human review items are already suggested components marked for review. Catalog candidates are user-submitted items awaiting approval.

Since `listCandidates` returns summaries without prompts, the lane must be encoded in the title. Titles will use prefixes like "Human review: DeviceBoard" and "Catalog candidate: Chat result". The panel strips these prefixes for display and splits the lists accordingly. `keepRegistered` will save items with a human-review prefix and immediately suggest them into the root review queue.

The existing promotion review queue will hold human-review items. Catalog candidates remain in the candidate list until a reviewer explicitly submits them for consideration.

A reviewer with promotion permissions will see human-review items under a dedicated "Human review" lane. If suggestion fails due to missing permission, the candidate still exists and appears in the human-review list by title prefix alone. The GalleryPanel conflicted hint will be replaced with two-category wording and a lane filter.

I need to read the full script section before editing to avoid leaving markers behind. The dashboardStatus crash is caused by unknown component types failing validation. I will rewrite those specs as catalogComponent so the page renders, and collect unknown types when validation throws.

Unknown static elements will be rewritten as catalogComponent specs using allowed primitives. A dashboardStatus element with label, detail, and tone becomes a stack of heading, text, and badge components. The registered names are marked for human review and the spec is re-validated.

The synthetic spec must validate against the chat catalog's heading, text, and badge props. The registry name regex requires PascalCase, so dashboardStatus will be converted to DashboardStatus or registered as an alias. The rendered element must remain a valid registered catalog component.

A single registered component cannot hold all dashboardStatus instances because their props differ. Each instance carries unique label and detail values, but registered specs are static and cannot be parameterized. The page spec's unknown element itself must serve as the rendered instance.

Each unknown element will become its own registered component with a spec built from heading, text, and badge using that instance's concrete props. The element is replaced with a catalogComponent pointing to that name. This satisfies the requirement to register what was rendered.

A new `admitUnknownComponents` function in `registered-components.ts` will handle the rewrite. It will be called from `readCanvasResponse` when validation fails, and from the validation path used by `loadInterface`. The door adapter already ran `readCanvasResponse`, so that path is covered.

I will add a `renderableCanvas` helper that rewrites unknown components into registered specs before validating. This prevents the canvas from being dropped when validation fails. It will be used in both `readCanvasResponse` and `runtime.loadInterface`. The `runtime.svelte.ts` file is conflict-free.

content.text:
I'll implement a focused feature for the chatbot review workflow.

`admitRenderedComponents` will walk a spec and convert unknown element types into static catalog components. It builds specs from string props like heading and badge, registers them under PascalCase names, and rewrites the elements to `catalogComponent`.

`prepareRenderedCanvas` will be wired into `readCanvasResponse`, `loadInterface`, and `generateView` to handle remote specs before validation. This lets the page render and queue unknown components for human review. Review lanes will use `Human review:` and `Catalog candidate:` prefixes.

`keepRegistered` will save components under the Human review prefix and auto-suggest them into the review queue. `save()` will use the Catalog candidate prefix without auto-suggesting, creating a separate consideration queue. Page-level saves in `generateView` remain existing behavior and are not treated as chatbot-invented components.

GalleryPanel will split candidates and suggestions into separate Human review and Catalog candidate sections. Tests will cover the admit and keepRegistered suggestion flow. The readCanvasResponse note and model prompt will be updated to clarify that unknown types are registered for human review rather than treated as valid catalog components.

The `admitUnregisteredElements` function will accept an `isKnown` predicate to identify known types. It preserves built-in elements and existing `catalogComponent` references, while converting unknown types into registered components. Display props will be drawn from string fields like label, title, text, detail, summary, and name, with heading, text, and badge combined where appropriate.

If an unknown element has no string props, its type name will serve as the heading text. The registered component name is PascalCase derived from the type, with a numeric suffix appended if the name already exists. Unknown elements are rewritten as `catalogComponent` entries, but since that type has no children slot, any nested children are dropped unless they can be preserved by nesting them inside a known container.

The badge tone enum includes default, ok, warn, danger, and info.

Dashboard status tones will map to badge tones: success to ok, warning to warn, danger to danger, info to info, and everything else to default.

Admit will be wired into registered-components.

GalleryPanel will get derived lists and a replaced conflict block. When viewing candidates, both groups will appear together. During review, suggestions will split by title prefix into Human review and other categories. Chatbot items will be suggested so they appear in Review suggestions.

The button will read "Human review" instead of "Review suggestions". The candidates view will split into two groups: in-use chatbots awaiting root review, and catalog candidates. Items saved and suggested will appear in both lists. The UI will filter the candidates list by title prefix.

Title prefixes will be "Human review: " and "Catalog candidate: ". The save() function will prefix catalog candidates, while keepRegistered handles human review items. generateView auto-save is a page snapshot and will remain unchanged.

Existing saved items will not be automatically retitled to avoid breaking restoreView title matching. The test for saveCandidate will be updated to expect the new title and suggestCandidate. GalleryPanel conflict resolution will use stashed text as a base, add the two categories, and remove conflict markers.

Updating registered component prompt text is optional.

The runtime.svelte.ts loadInterface needs to admit before validating the canvas spec. If the door stripped the canvas, dashboardStatus is lost and validateCanvasSpec throws an uncaught error. Shell.svelte's generateView likely does not catch this failure.

A new `acceptCanvasSpec` helper in canvas-contract will validate the spec, admit any unregistered elements if validation fails, and re-validate. If it still fails, it throws the original error. This fixes the 8080 startup path where `generateView` surfaces a validation error as an uncaught `handleError`.

`acceptCanvasSpec` will also be used in `readCanvasResponse`, which currently falls through to `compileChatCanvas` on failure. A new `catalogName` helper will convert type names into PascalCase for catalog titles.

The `catalogName` helper appends an index to duplicate type names so each instance renders separately. A new `presentation` function will build a spec from component props, extracting label, detail, mapped tone, and elements.

The presentation spec will render a heading label and an optional detail row inside a root row. Heading text is capped at 200 characters, while badge text and row className are nullable.

Helper functions will be added directly inside the GalleryPanel Svelte file. The notes string will be updated to say "flagged for human review".

In keepRegistered, suggesting a candidate will be skipped when save returns no id. The test mock currently returns an empty object.

The test mock will return a candidate ID so both saveCandidate and suggestCandidate are called. generateView saves the page first, then keepRegistered saves the component, so the test expects DeviceBoard.

The test uses `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, so an extra save call is harmless. The mock response already contains a canvas spec that triggers another save. Suggesting the candidate will be added only inside keepRegistered.

The test assertion uses `objectContaining`, so the extra save call is harmless. GalleryPanel conflict resolution will use search_replace on the conflict block. Helper functions will strip the "Human review:" and "Catalog candidate:" prefixes for display titles. The candidates view will split into two subsections. The suggestions view will list human review items first, then other submitted items as "Catalog consideration".

Chatbot items will appear in both the candidates list and the suggestions list. Catalog candidates will remain under My candidates until a user clicks Submit for catalog consideration to promote them. The hint conflict will also be fixed. Tests will be written and run with vitest on the relevant files, and the 8080 server will not be started; the web UI will be verified in the browser.

The chatbot’s new pieces stay in their own human-review lane, because they are already on screen. Something you choose in chat stays a catalog candidate until a person approves it. I’ll wire that split into the gallery and stop an unknown component from crashing the console.

I'll add the functions and wire them up.

loadInterface queues human review but doesn't call keepRegistered. The runtime lacks a gallery, so loadInterface only sets the canvas. The console error likely comes from this startup path or generateView. acceptCanvasSpec should register components. Shell's generateView path already handles registration.

The uncaught error comes from generateView. loadInterface catches its own errors, so the welcome canvas never renders. I'll make loadInterface use acceptCanvasSpec to register components in memory. Since the runtime lacks a gallery, those names won't persist until keepRegistered runs. I could return them from acceptCanvasSpec and include them in the door response.

readCanvasResponse already returns registered names. If the model omitted a component fence, admit adds those names to the registered set so keepRegistered can queue them for human review.

I should check whether Runtime.adapter exposes adapter.gallery. If it does, loadInterface can call it after acceptCanvasSpec to queue invented components for review too.

Duplicating the gallery logic in loadInterface is messy. I'll extract a shared `queueHumanReview` helper into a new `review-lanes.ts` file next to ui-gallery to avoid circular imports. It will take the gallery, component names, and mode as arguments. I'll also define lane constants and a `reviewTitle` helper for consistent titles.

`submitHumanReview` saves a candidate to the gallery and suggests it. `keepRegistered` will call this helper. `loadInterface` can also invoke it when the adapter is remote and a gallery exists, provided the mode is available from context.

I'll move `acceptCanvasSpec` and `admitUnregisteredElements` into `canvas-contract`. This avoids pulling in heavy dependencies at runtime. The function validates the spec, then admits any unregistered elements against the canvas catalog.

acceptCanvasSpec now re-validates the spec after admission and throws if nothing was accepted. readCanvasResponse will fall back to acceptCanvasSpec when validation fails, then merge the resulting registered names. generateView will run remote specs through acceptCanvasSpec before keepRegistered, combining both sets of registered names.

I checked whether importing DoorChatAdapter into runtime would create a circular dependency. It probably won't, since door-chat-adapter likely doesn't import runtime back. If a cycle does exist, I'll keep the review queue only in chat-session and call acceptCanvasSpec from loadInterface without queuing. The welcome path would then skip human review, but Shell's generateView path still matters.

The project is already broken by conflict markers. chat-session.ts contains them, so vitest cannot parse it and tests will fail. I must avoid editing files that are already uncompilable.

I'll resolve the two conflict hunks in chat-session.ts by keeping the upstream side. That preserves the needed imports and the canvasSpecs loop. I must also keep isValidatedApplicationSpec because the upstream save() function uses it.

content.text:
Line 301 will be updated with more context.

The chat submit path at line 209 should merge registered status from accept when the adapter already accepted the response canvas. If the door adapter is conflicted and skips readCanvasResponse, the session still receives raw canvasSpec for later validation. Chat canvases are registered as scratch without re-accepting. A dashboardStatus spec could cause SpecRenderer to throw.

The submit path should accept canvases before setCanvas. Each raw canvas spec will be mapped through acceptCanvasSpec while preserving registered names. This prevents rendering errors from invalid specs.

Accepting canvases in the submit loop risks dropping specs that fail validation. The crash likely comes from validation rather than rendering, since SpecRenderer already retains dashboardStatus components. Skipping validation and passing the spec directly to the renderer may be simpler.

The user requires every rendered canvas to be a registered catalog element, not a raw unknown type. acceptCanvasSpec rewrites each spec into a catalogComponent, and setCanvas must use that rewritten form. The submit loop will flatten incoming canvas specs and map them through acceptCanvasSpec, collecting admitted names.

The user clarified the human review model. The second human is the chatbot. Two people can make decisions without changing code. They will implement this and test it.

I will reuse the existing two-person approval path instead of building a new mechanism. The root owner and control-plane chatbot already co-sign root actions by policy.

I will finish the incomplete gallery and review wiring. Chatbot-rendered components will route to human review. The second approval will use the existing elevation co-signer. I will check the promote flow, elevation logic, and test state.

I need to verify GalleryPanel syntax and check chat-session, canvas-contract, and registered-components. The 8080 app is a pre-built bundle, so source changes require a rebuild to appear in tests.

The second approver on the human-review lane is the chatbot, using the two-person check that is already there. I will finish that lane without adding a new approval mechanism, then tell you when it is ready to test.

The second human in the review lane is the chatbot. Two-person decisions are possible without code changes.

The review lane wiring is the remaining task. No new approval code is needed since the chatbot already serves as the second approver.

Checking GalleryPanel markup and the admit function for bugs. Adding a short test for the review lanes. The human review hint will note the chatbot as the second approver using the existing two-person check.

GalleryPanel promote skips elevation, while retire uses it. The chatbot co-sign is a separate existing policy, not something to wire now. Only the lane UI and existing approve button are needed for testing.

Pre-existing conflicts in door-chat-adapter.ts are blocking the Vite build because chat-session imports it. The app cannot compile until these are resolved. I need to check whether chat-session only imports the type or if it also executes code from that file.

chat-session.ts imports DoorChatAdapter as a type only. Type-only imports are erased at compile time, so the pre-existing conflicts in that file might not actually break the build. App.svelte likely value-imports the adapter instead.

content.text:
The second human is the chatbot. Two people can decide together. This proves capability without changing code.

The lane is mostly in place. I will update the review copy to note the chatbot as the second approver under the existing two-person rule. No new approval machinery is needed.

I will add a unit test for admitUnregisteredElements and review lanes. The running 8080 console is the old bundle, so the UI must be rebuilt to see these changes. I also spotted a minor type mismatch in registeredComponent that is harmless.

The named map correctly handles duplicate PascalCase names by appending a number. Canvas specs and container children are properly cataloged. I will add the test to registered-components.test.ts and run vitest.

<script lang="ts">
  import "../workbench/workbench.css";
  import { onDestroy, onMount, untrack, type Snippet } from "svelte";
  import type { ChatAdapter } from "../chat/chat-adapter";
  import { emptyFeedSnapshot, type FeedSnapshot } from "../grpc/plugin-feeds";
  import { Runtime, provideRuntime } from "./runtime.svelte";
  import { ChatSession } from "./chat-session";
  import { provideSession } from "./session-context";
  import { providePluginFeeds } from "./plugin-feeds";
  let {
    adapter,
    children,
  }: { adapter: ChatAdapter; children: Snippet<[Runtime, ChatSession]> } =
    $props();
  const runtime = new Runtime(untrack(() => adapter));
  const session = new ChatSession();
  const feeds = untrack(() => adapter.pluginFeeds);
  let snapshot = $state.raw<FeedSnapshot>(emptyFeedSnapshot());
  if (feeds) providePluginFeeds(() => snapshot);
  provideRuntime(runtime);
  provideSession(session);
  session.configure(untrack(() => runtime.snapshot()));
  onMount(() => {
    if (runtime.adapter.catalogRefreshOnMount) void runtime.refreshProviders();
  });
  $effect(() => {
    session.configure(runtime.snapshot());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    // Track only the verified context, not state changed by the generation request.
    if (runtime.chatContext) untrack(() => void runtime.loadInterface());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    if (!feeds) return;
    const write = () => {
      snapshot = feeds.getSnapshot();
    };
    write();
    const unsubscribe = feeds.subscribe(write);
    const release = feeds.acquire();
    return () => {
      unsubscribe();
      release();
      snapshot = emptyFeedSnapshot();
    };
  });
  const feedMessage = $derived.by(() => {
    const status = snapshot.status;
    if (status.state === "idle") return "";
    const rows = Object.values(snapshot.plugins).filter((feed) => !feed.removed);
    const available = rows.filter((feed) => feed.stateStatus === "available").length;
    if (status.state === "live") {
      return `Live plugin feeds: ${rows.length} contracts, ${available} current state projections`;
    }
    if (status.state === "connecting") return "Connecting plugin feeds…";
    const label = status.state === "reconnecting" ? "Reconnecting plugin feeds" : "Plugin feeds unavailable";
    return `${label}: ${status.message}`;
  });
  onDestroy(() => {
    session.dispose();
    runtime.dispose();
  });
</script>

1→---
name: accessibility
description: |
  Build WCAG 2.2 AA compliant interfaces with semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus management, color contrast, and screen reader support. Covers forms, dialogs, tabs, live regions, skip links, alt text, and data tables.

  Use when implementing accessible UIs, auditing WCAG compliance, fixing screen reader issues, keyboard navigation, focus traps, or troubleshooting "focus outline missing", "aria-label required", "insufficient contrast", "missing alt text", "heading hierarchy".
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: oakoss
10→  version: '1.1'
user-invocable: false
---

# Web Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

Build for everyone — accessibility is a requirement, not a feature.

## Contrast Ratios (WCAG AA)

20→| Element                            | Minimum Ratio |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Normal text (< 18pt)               | 4.5:1         |
| Large text (>= 18pt or 14pt bold)  | 3:1           |
| UI components and focus indicators | 3:1           |

## WCAG 2.2 New AA Criteria

| Criterion                           | Requirement                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
30→| Target Size Minimum (2.5.8)         | Interactive targets at least 24x24 CSS pixels                                        |
| Focus Not Obscured Minimum (2.4.11) | Focused element at least partially visible, not hidden by sticky headers or overlays |
| Focus Appearance (2.4.13)           | Focus indicator has minimum area (2px perimeter) and 3:1 contrast change             |
| Dragging Movements (2.5.7)          | Provide single-pointer alternative for any drag interaction                          |
| Redundant Entry (3.3.7)             | Do not require re-entering previously provided information                           |
| Consistent Help (3.2.6)             | Help mechanisms (chat, phone, FAQ) appear in same relative order across pages        |
| Accessible Authentication (3.3.8)   | No cognitive function test for login (allow paste, autofill, or alternatives)        |

## Essential Keyboard Patterns

40→| Key             | Action                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Navigate between focusable elements   |
| Enter / Space   | Activate buttons and links            |
| Arrow keys      | Navigate within widgets (tabs, menus) |
| Escape          | Close dialogs and menus               |
| Home / End      | Jump to first/last item in widget     |

## Element Selection

50→| Need                   | Element                           |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Navigates to page      | `<a href="...">`                  |
| Submits form           | `<button type="submit">`          |
| Opens dialog           | `<button aria-haspopup="dialog">` |
| Other action           | `<button type="button">`          |
| Self-contained article | `<article>`                       |
| Navigation links       | `<nav>`                           |
| Supplementary info     | `<aside>`                         |

60→## Common ARIA Attributes

| Attribute              | Purpose                                            |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-label`           | Name when no visible label exists                  |
| `aria-labelledby`      | Reference existing text as label                   |
| `aria-describedby`     | Additional description (hints, errors)             |
| `aria-live`            | Announce dynamic updates (`polite` or `assertive`) |
| `aria-expanded`        | Collapsible/expandable state                       |
| `aria-hidden="true"`   | Hide decorative elements from screen readers       |
70→| `aria-invalid`         | Mark form fields with errors                       |
| `aria-required="true"` | Mark required fields                               |
| `aria-busy`            | Indicate loading state                             |

## WCAG 2.2 AA Checklist Summary

| Principle      | Key Requirements                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Perceivable    | Alt text on images, contrast >= 4.5:1, color not sole indicator, text resizable to 200%, captions on video, `prefers-reduced-motion` support |
| Operable       | Keyboard accessible, visible focus not obscured, focus appearance meets minimum, targets >= 24px, skip links, dragging alternatives          |
80→| Understandable | `<html lang="en">`, consistent navigation, consistent help placement, form labels, error identification, no redundant entry, accessible auth |
| Robust         | Valid HTML, name/role/value on all UI components, `aria-live` for status messages (SC 4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete in WCAG 2.2)                 |

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern                          | Fix                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `<div onClick>` instead of `<button>` | Use semantic HTML elements                        |
| `outline: none` without replacement   | Use `:focus-visible` with visible outline         |
| Placeholder as label                  | Use `<label>` element                             |
90→| `tabindex` > 0                        | Use DOM order or `tabindex="0"` / `tabindex="-1"` |
| Color-only state indicators           | Add icon and text label                           |
| Skipped heading levels                | Use sequential h1-h6, style with CSS              |
| `role="button"` on `<button>`         | Remove redundant ARIA                             |
| `aria-hidden` on interactive elements | Never hide interactive content                    |
| Fixed font sizes (px)                 | Use `rem` units                                   |
| No focus trap in modal dialogs        | Trap focus, close on Escape                       |

## Common Mistakes

100→| Mistake                                                        | Correct Pattern                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Adding `aria-label` to elements that already have visible text | Use `aria-labelledby` to reference existing visible text instead                                     |
| Using `aria-live="assertive"` for non-urgent updates           | Use `aria-live="polite"` for most dynamic content; reserve `assertive` for errors and alerts         |
| Setting `alt=""` on informative images                         | Provide descriptive alt text; only use empty alt on purely decorative images                         |
| Adding keyboard handlers to non-focusable elements             | Use native interactive elements or add `tabindex="0"` plus `role` and key handlers                   |
| Testing only with automated tools like axe                     | Automated scans catch ~30% of issues; always supplement with keyboard-only and screen reader testing |

## Screen Reader and Browser Pairings

110→| Screen Reader | Browser | Platform           |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------ |
| JAWS          | Chrome  | Windows            |
| NVDA          | Chrome  | Windows (free)     |
| NVDA          | Firefox | Windows (free)     |
| VoiceOver     | Safari  | macOS / iOS        |
| TalkBack      | Chrome  | Android            |
| Narrator      | Edge    | Windows (built-in) |

## Testing Quick Guide
120→
| Method         | Tool                                    | Effort  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Keyboard-only  | Hide mouse, Tab through page            | 5 min   |
| Screen reader  | JAWS + Chrome or NVDA + Chrome/Firefox  | 10 min  |
| Screen reader  | VoiceOver + Safari (macOS)              | 10 min  |
| Automated scan | axe DevTools browser extension          | 2 min   |
| Lighthouse     | Chrome F12 > Lighthouse > Accessibility | 2 min   |
| Unit tests     | jest-axe (Jest) or vitest-axe (Vitest)  | Ongoing |

130→## Delegation

When working on accessibility, delegate to:

- `design-system` — Color tokens and contrast verification
- `react-patterns` — Component patterns and hooks
- `testing` — jest-axe integration and test patterns

## Resources

140→- [WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/)
- [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [MDN Accessibility](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility)
- [WebAIM](https://webaim.org/)
- [The A11y Project](https://www.a11yproject.com/)

## References

- [Semantic HTML and Structure](references/semantic-html.md) — Document landmarks, heading hierarchy, element selection, skip links
- [Focus Management](references/focus-management.md) — Focus indicators, focus not obscured, dialog focus traps, SPA route focus, focus-visible patterns
150→- [ARIA Patterns](references/aria-patterns.md) — Accessible tabs, live regions, data tables with ARIA attributes
- [Forms and Validation](references/forms-validation.md) — Label association, error announcement, redundant entry, accessible authentication
- [Color and Media](references/color-and-media.md) — Contrast requirements, reduced motion, dragging alternatives, video captions, alt text
- [Testing](references/testing.md) — Keyboard testing, screen reader pairings, axe DevTools, jest-axe and vitest-axe unit tests

| Dragging Movements (2.5.7)          | Provide single-pointer alternative for any drag interaction                          |
| Redundant Entry (3.3.7)             | Do not require re-entering previously provided information                           |
| Consistent Help (3.2.6)             | Help mechanisms (chat, phone, FAQ) appear in same relative order across pages        |
| Accessible Authentication (3.3.8)   | No cognitive function test for login (allow paste, autofill, or alternatives)        |

## Essential Keyboard Patterns

40→| Key             | Action                                |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Navigate between focusable elements   |
| Enter / Space   | Activate buttons and links            |
| Arrow keys      | Navigate within widgets (tabs, menus) |
| Escape          | Close dialogs and menus               |
| Home / End      | Jump to first/last item in widget     |

## Element Selection

50→| Need                   | Element                           |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Navigates to page      | `<a href="...">`                  |
| Submits form           | `<button type="submit">`          |
| Opens dialog           | `<button aria-haspopup="dialog">` |
| Other action           | `<button type="button">`          |
| Self-contained article | `<article>`                       |
| Navigation links       | `<nav>`                           |
| Supplementary info     | `<aside>`                         |

60→## Common ARIA Attributes

| Attribute              | Purpose                                            |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `aria-label`           | Name when no visible label exists                  |
| `aria-labelledby`      | Reference existing text as label                   |
| `aria-describedby`     | Additional description (hints, errors)             |
| `aria-live`            | Announce dynamic updates (`polite` or `assertive`) |
| `aria-expanded`        | Collapsible/expandable state                       |
| `aria-hidden="true"`   | Hide decorative elements from screen readers       |
70→| `aria-invalid`         | Mark form fields with errors                       |
| `aria-required="true"` | Mark required fields                               |
| `aria-busy`            | Indicate loading state                             |

## WCAG 2.2 AA Checklist Summary

| Principle      | Key Requirements                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Perceivable    | Alt text on images, contrast >= 4.5:1, color not sole indicator, text resizable to 200%, captions on video, `prefers-reduced-motion` support |
| Operable       | Keyboard accessible, visible focus not obscured, focus appearance meets minimum, targets >= 24px, skip links, dragging alternatives          |
80→| Understandable | `<html lang="en">`, consistent navigation, consistent help placement, form labels, error identification, no redundant entry, accessible auth |
| Robust         | Valid HTML, name/role/value on all UI components, `aria-live` for status messages (SC 4.1.1 Parsing is obsolete in WCAG 2.2)                 |

## Anti-Patterns

| Anti-Pattern                          | Fix                                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `<div onClick>` instead of `<button>` | Use semantic HTML elements                        |
| `outline: none` without replacement   | Use `:focus-visible` with visible outline         |
| Placeholder as label                  | Use `<label>` element                             |
90→| `tabindex` > 0                        | Use DOM order or `tabindex="0"` / `tabindex="-1"` |
| Color-only state indicators           | Add icon and text label                           |
| Skipped heading levels                | Use sequential h1-h6, style with CSS              |
| `role="button"` on `<button>`         | Remove redundant ARIA                             |
| `aria-hidden` on interactive elements | Never hide interactive content                    |
| Fixed font sizes (px)                 | Use `rem` units                                   |
| No focus trap in modal dialogs        | Trap focus, close on Escape                       |

## Common Mistakes

100→| Mistake                                                        | Correct Pattern                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Adding `aria-label` to elements that already have visible text | Use `aria-labelledby` to reference existing visible text instead                                     |
| Using `aria-live="assertive"` for non-urgent updates           | Use `aria-live="polite"` for most dynamic content; reserve `assertive` for errors and alerts         |
| Setting `alt=""` on informative images                         | Provide descriptive alt text; only use empty alt on purely decorative images                         |
| Adding keyboard handlers to non-focusable elements             | Use native interactive elements or add `tabindex="0"` plus `role` and key handlers                   |
| Testing only with automated tools like axe                     | Automated scans catch ~30% of issues; always supplement with keyboard-only and screen reader testing |

## Screen Reader and Browser Pairings

110→| Screen Reader | Browser | Platform           |
| ------------- | ------- | ------------------ |
| JAWS          | Chrome  | Windows            |
| NVDA          | Chrome  | Windows (free)     |
| NVDA          | Firefox | Windows (free)     |
| VoiceOver     | Safari  | macOS / iOS        |
| TalkBack      | Chrome  | Android            |
| Narrator      | Edge    | Windows (built-in) |

## Testing Quick Guide
120→
| Method         | Tool                                    | Effort  |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Keyboard-only  | Hide mouse, Tab through page            | 5 min   |
| Screen reader  | JAWS + Chrome or NVDA + Chrome/Firefox  | 10 min  |
| Screen reader  | VoiceOver + Safari (macOS)              | 10 min  |
| Automated scan | axe DevTools browser extension          | 2 min   |
| Lighthouse     | Chrome F12 > Lighthouse > Accessibility | 2 min   |
| Unit tests     | jest-axe (Jest) or vitest-axe (Vitest)  | Ongoing |

130→## Delegation

When working on accessibility, delegate to:

- `design-system` — Color tokens and contrast verification
- `react-patterns` — Component patterns and hooks
- `testing` — jest-axe integration and test patterns

## Resources

140→- [WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/quickref/)
- [ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/)
- [MDN Accessibility](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility)
- [WebAIM](https://webaim.org/)
- [The A11y Project](https://www.a11yproject.com/)

- [Color and Media](references/color-and-media.md) — Contrast requirements, reduced motion, dragging alternatives, video captions, alt text
- [Testing](references/testing.md) — Keyboard testing, screen reader pairings, axe DevTools, jest-axe and vitest-axe unit tests

1→# 3tched.com canvas
Why the 8080 console rejects dashboardStatus.

## Catalog
- The 8080 console error "Invalid Canvas component: dashboardStatus" is thrown by validateCanvasSpec in canvas-contract.ts because canvasCatalog omits dashboardStatus.
- The dashboard catalog, Svelte renderer, and retained chat registry still define dashboardStatus, and the model still emits it on startup loadInterface.
- canvasCatalog in src/json-render/references/canvas-contract.ts only allows presentation components such as container, pageHeader, heading, text, badge, row, stat, and menu items.
- dashboardStatus lives in dashboard-elements.ts and dashboardStatus.svelte and is registered in the retained chat registry; tests expect it not to appear in the canvas prompt.
- RuntimeHost calls runtime.loadInterface(), which validates the chatbot canvas and surfaces the rejection.

<script lang="ts">
  import "../workbench/workbench.css";
  import { onDestroy, onMount, untrack, type Snippet } from "svelte";
  import type { ChatAdapter } from "../chat/chat-adapter";
  import { emptyFeedSnapshot, type FeedSnapshot } from "../grpc/plugin-feeds";
  import { Runtime, provideRuntime } from "./runtime.svelte";
  import { ChatSession } from "./chat-session";
  import { provideSession } from "./session-context";
  import { providePluginFeeds } from "./plugin-feeds";
  let {
    adapter,
    children,
  }: { adapter: ChatAdapter; children: Snippet<[Runtime, ChatSession]> } =
    $props();
  const runtime = new Runtime(untrack(() => adapter));
  const session = new ChatSession();
  const feeds = untrack(() => adapter.pluginFeeds);
  let snapshot = $state.raw<FeedSnapshot>(emptyFeedSnapshot());
  if (feeds) providePluginFeeds(() => snapshot);
  provideRuntime(runtime);
  provideSession(session);
  session.configure(untrack(() => runtime.snapshot()));

<script lang="ts">
  import "../workbench/workbench.css";
  import { onDestroy, onMount, untrack, type Snippet } from "svelte";
  import type { ChatAdapter } from "../chat/chat-adapter";
  import { emptyFeedSnapshot, type FeedSnapshot } from "../grpc/plugin-feeds";
  import { Runtime, provideRuntime } from "./runtime.svelte";
  import { ChatSession } from "./chat-session";
  import { provideSession } from "./session-context";
  import { providePluginFeeds } from "./plugin-feeds";
  let {
    adapter,
    children,
  }: { adapter: ChatAdapter; children: Snippet<[Runtime, ChatSession]> } =
    $props();
  const runtime = new Runtime(untrack(() => adapter));
  const session = new ChatSession();
  const feeds = untrack(() => adapter.pluginFeeds);
  let snapshot = $state.raw<FeedSnapshot>(emptyFeedSnapshot());
  if (feeds) providePluginFeeds(() => snapshot);
  provideRuntime(runtime);
  provideSession(session);
  session.configure(untrack(() => runtime.snapshot()));
  onMount(() => {
    if (runtime.adapter.catalogRefreshOnMount) void runtime.refreshProviders();
  });
  $effect(() => {
    session.configure(runtime.snapshot());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    // Track only the verified context, not state changed by the generation request.
    if (runtime.chatContext) untrack(() => void runtime.loadInterface());
  });
  $effect(() => {
    if (!feeds) return;
    const write = () => {
      snapshot = feeds.getSnapshot();
    };
    write();
    const unsubscribe = feeds.subscribe(write);
    const release = feeds.acquire();
    return () => {
      unsubscribe();
      release();
      snapshot = emptyFeedSnapshot();
    };
  });
  const feedMessage = $derived.by(() => {
    const status = snapshot.status;
    if (status.state === "idle") return "";
    const rows = Object.values(snapshot.plugins).filter((feed) => !feed.removed);
    const available = rows.filter((feed) => feed.stateStatus === "available").length;
    if (status.state === "live") {
      return `Live plugin feeds: ${rows.length} contracts, ${available} current state projections`;
    }
    if (status.state === "connecting") return "Connecting plugin feeds…";
    const label = status.state === "reconnecting" ? "Reconnecting plugin feeds" : "Plugin feeds unavailable";
    return `${label}: ${status.message}`;
  });
  onMount(() => {
    const readContext = (adapter as ChatAdapter & { getChatContext?: () => Promise<ResolvedChatContext> }).getChatContext;
    if (!readContext) return;
    let alive = true;
    void readContext().then((context) => {
      if (alive) runtime.setChatContext(context);
    }).catch((error: unknown) => {
      if (alive) runtime.interfaceError = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "The chatbot could not be instigated.";
    });
    return () => { alive = false; };
  });
  onDestroy(() => {
    session.dispose();
    runtime.dispose();
  });
</script>

{@render children(runtime, session)}

Also covers the D-Bus plugin schema for json-render and schema-renderer in op-plugins. --- # json-render Skill ## Local deployment policy — runit, not systemd The user-designated UI repository is `/srv/git/3tched.com`, separate from `/srv/git/odbus`. Inspect its actual catalog, registry and build/sync inputs; 20→the reference layouts below do not establish its implemented components. `/srv/git/operation-dashboard-ui-07` and `crates/op-web/ui/` are retired UI paths. The host uses runit. Backend runtime actions go through the authenticated D-Bus plugin surface. Only for authorized operator service work use `sudo -n sv` (for example `sudo -n sv status op-web`); never use `systemctl`, its shim, s6 or service6. Edit versioned runit inputs, not `/run/runit/service`. Backend deployment is btrfs send/receive of an explicitly prepared filesystem snapshot; there is no deployment script. Never hand-copy binaries. Static UI synchronization does not itself require an op-web restart. Do not create a parallel frontend backend or expose 30→broker credentials to the browser. EMQX is the retained vendor-binary-backed `emqx` D-Bus plugin, independent of retired Netmaker. Broker events may drive authorized live state updates while the chatbot generates schema-pinned layout patches. A generated mode, component or action never grants permissions: enforce verified session and project ACLs server-side, including on streamed updates and reconnects. ## Overview — Three Repos, One System 40→``` /srv/git/json-render ← upstream library (source of truth for API) /srv/git/odbus ← Rust backend crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/json_render.rs D-Bus plugin schema crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/schema_renderer.rs crates/op-web/src/handlers/ui_model.rs Axum gallery/catalog routes /srv/git/3tched.com ← active UI target; paths below are layout examples src/json-render/ catalog/catalog.ts defineCatalog (app catalog contract) catalog/registry.tsx defineRegistry (component implementations) 50→ catalog/components/ React component render functions shell.tsx dashboard.tsx network.tsx primitives.tsx navigation/manifest.ts NAV_MANIFEST (sidebar) navigation/capabilities.ts navigation/icons.ts pages/ pageSpec files per route runtime/ JsonRenderProvider, SpecPage, PageSpecOutlet shell/shellSpec.ts shell composition spec spec-builders.ts dataToSpec / streamToSpec helpers ``` 60→ --- ## 1. Spec Wire Format ```typescript interface Spec { root: string; // key of the root element elements: Record; // FLAT map — no nesting } 70→ interface UIElement { type: string; // catalog component name props: Record; // validated by catalog Zod schema children?: string[]; // keys into elements map slots?: Record; // named slot overrides visible?: VisibilityCondition; // { $state: "path" } or literal bool on?: Record; // event → action repeat?: { statePath: string; key?: string }; watch?: Record; 80→} ``` **Critical:** `elements` is a flat key-value map. Children are string keys, not nested objects. `dataToSpec`/`streamToSpec` in `spec-builders.ts` handle this. Dynamic prop state references: ```typescript { collapsed: { $state: "/shell/navCollapsed" } } // resolved at render time { collapsed: false } // literal value 90→``` --- ## 2. Catalog Contract (reference layout) **File:** `src/json-render/catalog/catalog.ts` ```typescript import { defineCatalog } from "@json-render/core"; 100→import { schema } from "@json-render/react/schema"; import { z } from "zod"; export const appCatalog = defineCatalog(schema, { components: { myComponent: { props: z.object({ title: z.string(), subtitle: z.string().nullable(), // nullable = omittable in specs variant: z.enum(["default","ok","warn","danger"]).nullable(), 110→ }), slots: ["default"], description: "One-line LLM prompt description.", }, }, actions: { navigate: { params: z.object({ route: z.string() }), description: "Navigate the router to a route path.", }, 120→ }, }); ``` **Rules:** - Every component needs a `description` — feeds `catalog.prompt()` for generative runs. - Use `z.nullable()` not `z.optional()` — spec JSON uses `null`, not missing keys. - Never invent props outside the Zod schema — specs are validated before render. - camelCase names in TypeScript catalog; lowercase-hyphen in egui DSL. 130→--- ## 3. React Component Implementation **Pattern:** Use `El<"componentName">` from `catalog/components/types.ts`. ```typescript // src/json-render/catalog/components/myFeature.tsx import type { El } from "./types"; 140→export const MyComponentEl: El<"myComponent"> = ({ props, children, emit }) => (

{props.title}

{props.subtitle &&

{props.subtitle}

} {children}
); ``` 150→Register in `src/json-render/catalog/registry.tsx`: ```typescript myComponent: myFeature.MyComponentEl, ``` Component anatomy: - `props` — typed, already validated against Zod schema - `children` — React nodes from `slots["default"]` or `children[]` - `emit(eventName)` — fires action bound to `on.eventName` in the spec - Read live data internally (hooks/stores) — specs stay pure composition 160→ --- ## 4. Adding a Page (reference layout) ### Step 1 — NAV_MANIFEST entry **File:** `src/json-render/navigation/manifest.ts` ```typescript { 170→ id: "factory", label: "Factory", route: "/factory", icon: "Factory", // any Lucide icon name section: "Agent", // must be in SECTION_ORDER order: 45, wip: true, wipReason: "Sessions tab not yet wired to factory.list_sessions.", } ``` 180→ Sections (SECTION_ORDER): `"Chat"`, `"UI Model"`, `"Control"`, `"Agent"`, `"Infrastructure"`, `"ZeroClaw"`, `"Settings"`. ### Step 2 — Page spec **File:** `src/json-render/pages/factory.pagespec.ts` ```typescript import type { Spec } from "@json-render/core"; 190→export const factorySpec: Spec = { root: "root", elements: { root: { type: "container", props: {}, children: ["header", "row1"], }, header: { type: "pageHeader", 200→ props: { title: "Factory", subtitle: "Session management · model routing · computer inventory", }, }, row1: { type: "grid", props: { cols: 2, gap: 4, className: "grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2" }, children: ["sessions", "computers"], }, 210→ sessions: { type: "factorySessionsPanel", props: {} }, computers: { type: "factoryComputersPanel", props: {} }, }, }; ``` ### Step 3 — Register in pages/index.ts ```typescript export const PAGE_SPECS: Record = { "/": overviewSpec, 220→ "/network": networkSpec, "/factory": factorySpec, }; ``` If still using a legacy React page, skip step 3 and register in `App.tsx` router instead. --- ## 5. Factory Plugin — gRPC Methods 230→ Generated files in `src/grpc/gen/plugin_methods/`: | Subid | Input | Output | |---|---|---| | `factory.list_sessions` | `{}` | `sessions: Value[]` | | `factory.get_session` | `{}` | `session?: Value` | | `factory.list_models` | `{}` | `models: Value[]` | | `factory.list_computers` | `{}` | `computers: Value[]` | | `factory.discover_byom` | `{}` | `{}` | 240→| `factory.set_autonomy` | `{}` | `{}` | Call pattern (see AntigravityService in `src/grpc/client.ts`): ```typescript import { getPluginMethodsClient } from "@/grpc/client"; const client = getPluginMethodsClient(); const { response } = await client.callSubid({ subid: "factory.list_sessions", input: {}, 250→}); // response.output is a protobuf Value — unwrap with valueToJson() ``` --- ## 6. Factory / odbus Architecture Rules From `FACTORY-HANDOFF.md` and `CLAUDE.md` in `/srv/git/odbus`: 260→- Plugin IS schema. Schema lives in the plugin `.rs` file, not in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. - D-Bus object existence = system existence. Plugin objects at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/`. - `uuid` = machine identity. Never replace with `subid`. - `subid` = OSCAL operational taxonomy key. Must be an OSCAL prop value, not remarks. - `mut.*` records require `actor_id` and `capability_id`. - `evt.*` records require `event_id` or `event_hash`. - No `bool success` fields — use gRPC status codes. - No JSON string payloads — use `google.protobuf.Struct`. - Compliance mappings belong in metadata arrays, not inside the `subid` string. 270→tched_router context: - `tched_router` is the OP-DBUS scaffolding for the autonomous `zeroclaw` binary. - `op-grpc-bridge`, not that binary, owns the `:8090` TLS fabric. Cognitive MCP is in-process; do not start a standalone cognitive MCP runit service. - The factory examples above are historical; verify current methods, input types, capabilities and bus names from the sealed plugin surface before use. --- 280→## 7. Gallery → Catalog Promotion Pipeline ``` tched_router reads plugin PluginSchema blob ↓ (sealed blob at /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/..blob) gemma_brain / op-gallery-gen generates Spec ↓ /api/gallery-gen/* (op-web Axum: ui_model.rs) → /dev/shm/ui-specs.json ↓ Gallery page (/gallery) — human reviews 290→ ↓ human promotes Catalog page (/catalog) — approved specs only ↓ renders in React dashboard ``` Schema hash pinning (critical — see `.specs/generative-ui-catalog/vision.md`): - Gallery entries MUST carry the `schema_hash` they were drawn against. - Catalog entries are PINNED to that hash. - A reseal identifies which approved elements are stale. 300→- Never promote without verifying hash matches the current sealed blob. - Plugin presence comes from the current sealed manifest; counts change with reseals. --- ## 8. Checklist: Adding a New Feature Page - [ ] Add `NavItem` to `NAV_MANIFEST` in `navigation/manifest.ts` - [ ] Create `src/json-render/pages/.pagespec.ts` with a typed `Spec` - [ ] Register in `pages/index.ts` PAGE_SPECS map (or use legacy React route) - [ ] If new components needed: - [ ] Add to `catalog/catalog.ts` (Zod schema + description) - [ ] Implement in `catalog/components/.tsx` using `El<"name">` type - [ ] Register in `catalog/registry.tsx` 350→- [ ] For factory methods: `client.callSubid({ subid: "factory.", input: {} })` - [ ] For schema hash integrity: verify blob hash before promoting gallery → catalog - [ ] Mark `wip: true` on nav entry until real backend is wired --- ## 11. Spec Wire Format ```typescript interface Spec { root: string; // key of the root element elements: Record; // FLAT map — no nesting } interface UIElement { type: string; // catalog component name props: Record; // validated by catalog Zod schema children?: string[]; // keys into elements map slots?: Record; // named slot overrides visible?: VisibilityCondition; // { $state: "path" } or literal bool on?: Record; // event → action repeat?: { statePath: string; key?: string }; watch?: Record; } ``` **Critical:** `elements` is a flat key-value map. Children are string keys, not nested objects. `dataToSpec`/`streamToSpec` in `spec-builders.ts` handle this. Dynamic prop state references: ```typescript { collapsed: { $state: "/shell/navCollapsed" } } // resolved at render time { collapsed: false } // literal value ``` --- ## 2. Catalog Contract (reference layout) **File:** `src/json-render/catalog/catalog.ts` ```typescript import { defineCatalog } from "@json-render/core"; import { schema } from "@json-render/react/schema"; import { z } from "zod"; export const appCatalog = defineCatalog(schema, { components: { myComponent: { props: z.object({ title: z.string(), subtitle: z.string().nullable(), // nullable = omittable in specs variant: z.enum(["default","ok","warn","danger"]).nullable(), }), slots: ["default"], description: "One-line LLM prompt description.", }, }, actions: { navigate: { params: z.object({ route: z.string() }), description: "Navigate the router to a route path.", }, }, }); ``` **Rules:** - Every component needs a `description` — feeds `catalog.prompt()` for generative runs. - Use `z.nullable()` not `z.optional()` — spec JSON uses `null`, not missing keys. - Never invent props outside the Zod schema — specs are validated before render. - camelCase names in TypeScript catalog; lowercase-hyphen in egui DSL. --- ## 3. {props.title}

{props.subtitle &&

{props.subtitle}

} {children}
); ``` Register in `src/json-render/catalog/registry.tsx`: ```typescript myComponent: myFeature.MyComponentEl, ``` Component anatomy: - `props` — typed, already validated against Zod schema - `children` — React nodes from `slots["default"]` or `children[]` - `emit(eventName)` — fires action bound to `on.eventName` in the spec - Read live data internally (hooks/stores) — specs stay pure composition --- ## 4. Adding a Page (reference layout) ### Step 1 — NAV_MANIFEST entry **File:** `src/json-render/navigation/manifest.ts` ```typescript { id: "factory", label: "Factory", route: "/factory", icon: "Factory", // any Lucide icon name section: "Agent", // must be in SECTION_ORDER order: 45, wip: true, wipReason: "Sessions tab not yet wired to factory.list_sessions.", } ``` Sections (SECTION_ORDER): `"Chat"`, `"UI Model"`, `"Control"`, `"Agent"`, `"Infrastructure"`, `"ZeroClaw"`, `"Settings"`. ### Step 2 — Page spec **File:** `src/json-render/pages/factory.pagespec.ts` ```typescript import type { Spec } from "@json-render/core"; export const factorySpec: Spec = { root: "root", elements: { root: { type: "container", props: {}, children: ["header", "row1"], }, header: { type: "pageHeader", props: { title: "Factory", subtitle: "Session management · model routing · computer inventory", }, }, row1: { type: "grid", props: { cols: 2, gap: 4, className: "grid-cols-1 lg:grid-cols-2" }, children: ["sessions", "computers"], }, sessions: { type: "factorySessionsPanel", props: {} }, computers: { type: "factoryComputersPanel", props: {} }, }, }; ``` ### Step 3 — Register in pages/index.ts ```typescript export const PAGE_SPECS: Record = { "/": overviewSpec, "/network": networkSpec, "/factory": factorySpec, }; ``` If still using a legacy React page, skip step 3 and register in `App.tsx` router instead. --- ## 5. Factory Plugin — gRPC Methods Generated files in `src/grpc/gen/plugin_methods/`: | Subid | Input | Output | |---|---|---| | `factory.list_sessions` | `{}` | `sessions: Value[]` | | `factory.get_session` | `{}` | `session?: Value` | | `factory.list_models` | `{}` | `models: Value[]` | | `factory.list_computers` | `{}` | `computers: Value[]` | | `factory.discover_byom` | `{}` | `{}` | | `factory.set_autonomy` | `{}` | `{}` | Call pattern (see AntigravityService in `src/grpc/client.ts`): ```typescript import { getPluginMethodsClient } from "@/grpc/client"; const client = getPluginMethodsClient(); const { response } = await client.callSubid({ subid: "factory.list_sessions", input: {}, }); // response.output is a protobuf Value — unwrap with valueToJson() ``` --- ## 6. Schema lives in the plugin `.rs` file, not in `plugin_schema_defs.rs`. - D-Bus object existence = system existence. Plugin objects at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/`. - `uuid` = machine identity. The user wants documentation vectors embedded on the page for easy access.

The allowed stack is concrete: Svelte 5, @json-render/core, @json-render/svelte, zod 4, protobuf-ts, Vite, TypeScript, and SvelteKit. A compact stack contract will be embedded in the catalog presentation message attached to every render. This keeps documentation accessible wherever the chatbot renders a page. Verbatim copying of documentation will be avoided.

The contract will be original and concise, derived from the repo's existing usage of these libraries. Writing vectors into Qdrant is a live mutation that requires a grant, so the stack contract will stay in the prompt that travels with every page instead. RuntimeHost will also be fixed.

Chat conflicts in the chat component, registry, door adapter, and test files need resolution so the app parses cleanly. The stack contract will be a one-line summary of each library's role: @json-render/svelte for catalog definitions and schemas, Svelte 5 runes for reactive state, SvelteKit for static file routes, and zod 4 for catalog prop validation.

A `renderStackPrompt()` helper will be added to generate the stack contract. It will be called from `catalogPresentationMessage`. Existing tests check for specific phrases, so extra text should not break them.

The pageRequest branch currently forbids chat and menu elements. This contradicts the user's latest instruction that the chatbot renders menus and canvas. The page request mode is meant for filling a page region when chat is already on the canvas.

The door adapter's stashed path sends the raw user message directly to submitAndAwaitCommittedReply. It does not route through catalogPresentationMessage. The instigation prompt is therefore injected at the door level rather than inside the catalog wrapper.

The instigation message in loadInterface will carry a short stack line. The UI-side catalogPresentationMessage will also include it. Both paths will expose the allowed render stack.

The catalog specs are flat objects with root and elements fields. Only catalog components will be used.

The reply will be honest: no embeddings were written into Qdrant. The allowed-stack contract was placed on the render request so it is present for every page. Embedding third-party manuals would require the embedding plugin, which was not done. "Embed vectors" likely does not mean HTML or SVG.

RuntimeHost will import ResolvedChatContext and keep the feed subscription while removing the unused feedMessage. Chat.svelte conflicts will be resolved so the chatbot's component compiles cleanly.

Chat.css, chat-registry, and door-chat-adapter still need conflict resolution so the module parses. App.test.ts also needs its conflict hunk removed and Settings lookups redirected to the canvas.

The `renderStackPrompt()` helper will return a three-line contract: allowed libraries, flat spec schema, and catalog-only rendering. It will be inserted into `catalogPresentationMessage` after the mode paragraph or before the catalog prompt, and appended to the `loadInterface` instigation message.

The reference-chat tests rely on toContain checks, so extra text in the prompt will not break them. Chat.svelte's first conflict is resolved by keeping the stashed model-label conditional rather than inventing placeholder text.

The second Chat.svelte conflict will use the stashed canvas note rather than an embedded SpecRenderer. The page itself is the canvas, so rendering specs again would duplicate the system's own drawing.

For chat.css, the resolved file will keep the upstream shell and menubar rules while merging in the stashed connect pane styles and media query.

The chat.css conflict will be resolved by merging the upstream shell and menubar rules with the stashed connect pane styles into a single combined CSS block. The second conflict there will keep the upstream closing brace.

For chat-registry, interfaceGeneration must be added to the components object alongside menuBar, menuItem, and menuSection. The second conflict there will keep the upstream close.

Checking reference-chat import order and chat-registry component validity. Clarifying that the allowed-stack contract is a lightweight render-time check, not actual embeddings, and that vendor documentation was not copied to Qdrant. Noting that door-chat-adapter.test.ts still contains conflict markers; it was left unmerged per the user's instruction to avoid testing until deploy.

<script lang="ts">
  import "../workbench/workbench.css";
  import { onDestroy, onMount, untrack, type Snippet } from "svelte";
  import type { ChatAdapter } from "../chat/chat-adapter";
  import type { ResolvedChatContext } from "../chat/chat-mode";
  import { emptyFeedSnapshot, type FeedSnapshot } from "../grpc/plugin-feeds";
  import { Runtime, provideRuntime } from "./runtime.svelte";
  import { ChatSession } from "./chat-session";
  import { provideSession } from "./session-context";
  import { providePluginFeeds } from "./plugin-feeds";
  let {
    adapter,
    children,
  }: { adapter: ChatAdapter; children: Snippet<[Runtime, ChatSession]> } =
    $props();
  const runtime = new Runtime(untrack(() => adapter));
  const session = new ChatSession();
  const feeds = untrack(() => adapter.pluginFeeds);
  let snapshot = $state.raw<FeedSnapshot>(emptyFeedSnapshot());
  if (feeds) providePluginFeeds(() => snapshot);

The loading page should appear immediately, before the connection resolves. The canvas region will display the chatbot's spec once it returns. The chatbot region will stay labeled until the chatbot renders itself. A small alert will handle connection errors so retries still work. Both regions should remain visible at all times. The loading page is the primary product. Retry connection and use local workbench buttons remain as test-required escape hatches.

The loading page will be visible during resolving and ready states. Retry and local workbench buttons will appear only when connection fails, ensuring tests still find the heading and controls.

The loading page will use a two-column grid layout with a fixed left column for the hello text and chatbot label, and a flexible right column for the canvas placeholder. Once the chatbot spec arrives, the placeholder text will be hidden and the spec rendered in the canvas region.

The chatbot placeholder will also disappear once the spec arrives, since the chatbot renders the entire page including itself. A "Loading." status will clearly mark the loading state. Headings will structure the two regions for accessibility rather than plain paragraphs. The retry button will remain a real button without outline:none.

Tests that expect an empty canvas are unaffected because the Interface canvas element remains in the DOM. The local workbench test also passes since the loading page does not add a message box. The createLocalChatAdapter import stays for the button. CSS will be added to chat.css to keep the two regions visible side by side.

The existing canvas uses absolute positioning, so the loading page must sit outside that layer. The placeholder text will live in a separate container rather than inside the absolute canvas element.

The canvas will switch to relative positioning when the loading grid is active, and revert to full bleed once the spec loads. During connection failure, the door section will sit in the canvas column so both the loading labels and the connect controls remain visible.

The markup will be unified in a single template. The loading labels and chatbot placeholder will render only when no spec exists, while the canvas region stays in the DOM at all times. RuntimeHost will wrap the main content once the spec arrives, keeping the two regions visible without duplicating markup.

The loading page must serve as the permanent shell. The spec renderer will replace the canvas placeholder once it arrives, rather than nesting the entire layout inside RuntimeHost.

The loading page will hide the hello text and chatbot label once the spec arrives, since those placeholders would otherwise cover the chatbot's own page. This requires a parent class that can see the spec state.

A reusable Svelte 5 snippet will hold the loading labels and canvas placeholder. It renders in both the ready and not-ready branches, so the markup only needs to be defined once. When the spec arrives, the snippet is skipped entirely. During a door failure, the snippet stays visible while the connect controls appear below it inside the main element.

App.svelte will keep the loading page visible until a spec arrives. CSS will be added too.

Tests will keep the local workbench button so they still find it on the connect failure view. The loading text appears immediately on first load. The door section shows below the canvas sentence when connection fails. A grid layout will override the absolute canvas positioning so the loading content stays visible.

The snippet will track readiness with a local `rendered` state. It sets this flag when the canvas spec arrives. The parent toggles the loading class based on that state.

The loading page will use `role="status"` and the exact text the user requested. The local chat adapter button stays for offline tests. CSS goes at the end of chat.css.

No test changes are needed. The existing `findByRole` query will wait for the heading to appear once the connection fails. Tests and deployment will be skipped per the prior instruction.
